where: /en/people, 1440px, Prizic Demo (5 active members, 1 Property)
observed: A person's Property reach can only be set while inviting. On an existing member the row's "..." menu offers only "Remove access" (plus "New invitation link" while an invitation is pending), and the Properties column is plain text. Yet the invite dialog warns "They can sign in, but they will see nothing until you assign one", and the Add back and Remove access copy say the same ("they reach no Property until you assign one"). Nobody can assign one from this screen. The staff module has assignProperty/unassignProperty (approved rows SP-S1-18, -19, -28) but no workspace code calls them.
expected: Whatever the copy promises is reachable: the owner can add or remove a Property for a member on the roster, with the consequence named, because a person invited with no Property, or added back after leaving, is otherwise locked out of everything.
suggested_fix: Make the Properties cell a multi-picker like the role picker (prefilled from the row, confirm names that sessions end), or add "Change Properties" to the row menu. Until then, remove the sentence that promises it.

where: Check-out dialog from /en/departures: Derya Polat (room 103, 6 days overdue, TRY 7,330) and Freya Andersen (room 308, 1 day overdue, TRY 0.00); both bookings were taken without a price
observed: Two notices sit one above the other: 'The departure is recorded as today, and the nights since then are charged to the bill' and then 'This booking was taken without a price, so its nights are not charged.' They contradict each other. For the guest at TRY 0.00 the dialog then says 'Nothing to pay. Their Folio is settled. One press and they are checked out', although six days or one night went uncharged. 'Settled' is a money statement the desk will repeat to the guest.
expected: One notice that is true for this booking: 'Overdue since Oct 23. The booking has no price, so nothing is charged for the extra nights.' 'Nothing to pay' should say 'No price on the booking, nothing charged' when that is why the balance is zero.
suggested_fix: Choose the overdue sentence by whether the booking is priced; replace 'Their Folio is settled' with a line that names the unpriced booking.

where: Check-out dialog at 1440 x 900, English
observed: The sentence 'A check-out cannot be taken back, so review the bill first' is in the dialog description marked screen-reader-only (sr-only in check-out-dialog.tsx); it does not appear on screen. The visible dialog never says the check-out is final. For a guest who owes money the notice 'The room is marked dirty...' is below the fold (dialog 1044 px tall in an 846 px box), so it and the quick picks need a scroll. The footer button is the only visible cue.
expected: The one irreversible action of the day names its consequence before the click, in view: 'This cannot be undone. The room is marked dirty.'
suggested_fix: Show the 'cannot be taken back' line as the first visible notice or beside the confirm button, and keep the confirm footer in view with the room notice above the reason box.

where: /en/room-calendar, click an overdue bar (Derya Polat, 103), 1280 px as Front desk, Manager and Owner, also /tr at 1280 and /en at 375 px as Front desk. Staging: at least 22 of the 38 bars are overdue, so this is the common state here.
observed: The details drawer is 384 px wide but its content is 627 px wide (measured: scrollWidth 627, clientWidth 383). Every right-aligned value (Arrived, Was due to leave, Overdue days, Nights, Reservation code, the balance TRY 7,330.00) and the whole 'Open in Departures' link are pushed off the right edge; only a hidden sideways scroll shows them. At 375 px the drawer is 281 px wide and 'Move Guest' is also half off screen. The confirmed-booking drawer (Amelia Taylor) fits, so only the overdue layout breaks, most likely because the three footer actions plus the long balance note sit in a no-wrap row.
expected: Every drawer shows its labels with their values at any width, and the actions wrap.
suggested_fix: Let the action row wrap (flex-wrap) and the balance note break onto its own line; add overflow-x-hidden on the drawer so a clipped value can never hide. Add a browser assertion that the overdue drawer has scrollWidth equal to clientWidth at 1280 and 375.

where: /en/room-calendar drawer for Amelia Taylor (304, Confirmed, Oct 19 to Oct 23, today Oct 24); /en/rooms tile dialog for 312 ('A guest arrives here on Oct 23, 2026').
observed: A booking whose arrival date has passed and who never checked in still reads as a normal Confirmed booking: 'Arrives Oct 19, 2026', no lateness, no Check in, no No-show. The Rooms dialog for 312 says 'A guest arrives here on Oct 23' on Oct 24. The room stays held (it is also the cause of CALENDAR-02), and these bookings only surface at Close the day, one day at a time. Same root as FO-02 and FO-06 of the 2026-10-22 front-office report, which still reproduces.
expected: A confirmed booking past its arrival says 'Due Oct 19, 5 days late', in the drawer, on the bar's spoken label and in the Rooms tile wording, and the drawer offers the next step.
suggested_fix: Tweak (now): say 'was due Oct 19, 5 days ago' in the drawer, the bar label and the Rooms tile dialog; use past tense. New interaction (already filed as RC-S5-03, deferred RC-DEF-04): Check in and No-show from the drawer.

where: /en/rooms as Front desk: no 'Add rooms' button, but the Block room dialog opens from every tile.
observed: 'Add rooms' is correctly hidden, but the Block room dialog is not gated: Front desk gets the full form with a required reason and a 'Block room' button. Code: handleSelectUnit does not read mayConfigure, which only controls Add. Whether the submit is refused by the database for this role is inferred from RB-S3-09 (approved) and not tested, because submitting is forbidden in this audit. The dialog also uses 'unit' while the page says 'room'.
expected: A role without permission to block is shown 'Report a problem' only, with the reason, and not a form that fails after typing.
suggested_fix: Pass mayConfigure to the block dialog; without it show only 'Report a problem' and say 'Only managers can block a room'.

where: /en/branding, 1440 px, Organization never branded
observed: A logo of 300 x 64 px (below the stated 128 px minimum) is accepted by the screen: it previews, the Save button turns on, and nothing says the file is too short. The screen shows no file size, no dimensions and no type check. The 128 px, 512 KB and type rules are only judged by the server after Save (code comment in branding-view.tsx: 'a logo's size is the server's to judge'), so the Owner learns the file is wrong after a round trip, with the error printed in the Logo card while Save sits in the Preview card at the bottom. I stopped before Save, so the exact refusal wording is unverified.
expected: The constraints are checked as the file is chosen, on the card where it was chosen, with the actual numbers.
suggested_fix: Read the image in the browser when it is chosen (width, height, bytes, type) and show 'logo.png, 300 x 64 px, 12 KB: needs to be at least 128 px tall' beside the field, keep Save off until it passes. Keep the server check as the authority.

where: /en/branding, with an unsaved colour and a chosen logo
observed: I typed a colour, chose a logo and clicked the Back arrow: the page left at once with no prompt and both drafts were lost. Configuration warns in the same situation (a leave-without-saving confirm fired when I clicked a sidebar link with an edited Property name), so two sibling settings screens behave differently. Branding is the one where a lost draft costs the most, because the logo has to be picked again.
expected: Branding warns before discarding a draft, the way Configuration and the housekeeping setting do.
suggested_fix: Use the same unsaved-changes guard (useUnsavedChangesGuard, already used in inspection-settings.tsx) on BrandingView when dirty.

where: /en/branding, Organization with a saved logo or colour (code); not pressed
observed: 'Reset to default' runs resetBranding on one click with no confirmation, no consequence sentence and no undo (onClick={reset} in branding-view.tsx). It removes the logo and the colour for every guest at every Property at once; the logo has to be uploaded again. I did not press it because the Organization has no brand to reset, so this is read from code.
expected: A change that every guest sees, and that loses a file, names its consequence and can be undone or confirmed in one click.
suggested_fix: A one-click confirm: 'Guests will see Ranza's mark and green theme. The logo is removed.' with Cancel / Reset, or keep the old brand for 10 seconds behind an Undo.

where: /en/data-export, Schedules tab
observed: From the code: a schedule row shows 'Active' and 'Next run: ...' but no last run time or outcome. The form says a schedule exports every date each time, and EXP-DEF-05 records that such a schedule 'may fail too_large'. A schedule whose runs fail therefore looks healthy; the person has to open History and match runs by date to find out. No schedules existed on staging, so this is read from export-schedules-table.tsx.
expected: The schedule row says when it last ran and whether that run worked, with a link to the file.
suggested_fix: Add 'Last run: 07:00 today, ready' or 'Last run failed: too large' with a link to the History row.

where: /en/analytics (October 2026) vs /en/analytics?month=2026-09, en, 1440px
observed: October says 'September 2026 had no activity, so there is nothing to compare with.' The September page shows 2 occupied nights, occupancy 6.7%, and 'Incomplete · 4 of 10 days were never closed'. The wording changed since the 10-11 audit, the claim is still wrong. '4 of 10 days' also does not say what the 10 are (September has 30 days).
expected: The comparison line is true: either it compares, or it says September has too little closed data to compare.
suggested_fix: Replace 'had no activity' with the real reason (no closed days with revenue) when nights exist, and state the denominator of 'of 10 days'.

where: /en/finance?folio=<id>, 'Add a charge' form, en, 1440px; stopped before submit
observed: Add a charge posts on one click of 'Post'. The only consequence text is under the form: 'A charge can be reversed with a reason, never deleted.' There is no sentence naming the guest, room and amount before it is posted ('Post TRY 1,250.00 to Derya Polat, 103?'), unlike Record payment ('Records TRY 7,330.00 paid by Cash for Derya Polat, 103') and Reverse (names the new balance and 'cannot be undone'). A mistyped 12500 for 1250 posts and then needs a reversal with a reason. I did not press Post. Basis: the dialog-less form seen on screen plus ChargeForm in folio-forms.tsx, which submits directly.
expected: A charge is money on a guest's bill; the one-click confirm that payment and reversal already have applies here too.
suggested_fix: Show the same one-sentence summary under the form as the amount is typed ('Adds TRY 1,250.00 to Derya Polat, 103'), and offer an Undo for 10 seconds after posting.

where: /en/accept-invitation?token=..., state "signed in as somebody else" (other_account); sign-in page while signed in
observed: When a colleague opens an invitation on a machine where someone else is signed in, the page says "Sign out, then open the link again" but shows only a "Go to sign in" button. I verified that /en/sign-in with a live session redirects straight to Today, so the button leads back into the other person's workspace. The page is outside the workspace shell, so it has no sign-out control. I could not mint a token, so the page state itself is read from code (invitation.ts, invitation-refused.tsx, messages), not seen.
expected: The page offers the one action it asks for: a "Sign out and continue" button that ends the other session and returns to this same link.
suggested_fix: In the other_account state replace "Go to sign in" with a sign-out action that redirects back to /accept-invitation?token=...; hotel front desks share machines, so this state is common, not rare.

where: /en/reservations > New reservation at 375 px (emulated mobile, 375 x 800)
observed: The dialog is 343 px wide but its form is 383 px wide (scrollWidth 383 vs clientWidth 343), so the right 40 px is cut off: the REQUIRED and OPTIONAL badges, the right edge of every input, and the arrow of Create reservation are clipped. The close button stays visible.
expected: The form fits the dialog at 375 px.
suggested_fix: Constrain the form grid to 100% of the dialog (min-w-0 on grid children, no fixed px padding wider than the dialog).

where: /en/today left open after the session ended (verified as Manager: session deleted with the app's own sign-out request, tab left open 65 s)
observed: Following a link after the session ended is handled well: sign-in page with "Sign in to carry on where you were." and the address kept. But a tab left open on Today, which polls every 60 s and is meant to stay open for a shift, only shows an amber "Couldn't refresh · showing 13:24". Nothing says you were signed out, there is no Sign in link, and the Check out buttons stay live. A desk that returns after lunch learns about it when an action fails. What those actions say was not tested (submitting is forbidden).
expected: A refresh answered 401 sends the person to sign-in with the return address, or shows "You were signed out. Sign in".
suggested_fix: Treat 401 from /api/today as session ended: redirect to /sign-in?next= or show a blocking banner with Sign in.

where: /en/today at 1440 px; Timeline vs Overview vs Housekeeping role's Today
observed: 'Dirty' and 'Clean, awaiting inspection' have two meanings. Front desk Timeline tile and Rooms card: '3 awaiting inspection, 8 dirty' (vacant rooms only, 13 vacant). Overview rooms card and the Housekeeping role's tiles: 'Dirty 17, Clean awaiting inspection 16' (includes rooms with a guest in them). Same word, same page, 8 versus 17. The 10-22 front-office report saw the same split between Today and Housekeeping.
expected: A figure with one name has one meaning. Where both are useful, name them: 'Dirty, vacant 8' and 'Dirty, all rooms 17'.
suggested_fix: Split the label wherever the occupied-room variant appears (Overview and the Housekeeping focus), or move all Today figures to the vacant-room definition and keep the all-rooms count on the Housekeeping board only.

where: /en/today Timeline, Rooms card, 1440 px
observed: The Rooms card headline says '42 can be sold tonight.' beside 29 guests in house, 2 rooms ready and the tile above reading 'Rooms ready to sell 2 / 42'. The sentence is the count of rooms that are not out of service (code: 'sellable'), not availability. A desk agent asked 'can I sell a room tonight?' will read 42.
expected: The headline answers the question it appears to answer, or says what it counts.
suggested_fix: Replace with the number that matters ('13 vacant rooms tonight, 2 ready') or relabel the 42 'rooms in service'.

where: /en/today Night desk, 'Before you hand over', 1440 px; 22 overdue guests owing TRY 92,160.00
observed: The hand-over list has two items: '2 arrivals have not come' and '13 days are waiting to be closed'. The 22 overdue departures, TRY 92,160.00 owed and 27 still to leave, which the waterfall above it shows as -27, are not handed over. In code (night-layout.tsx) the balances item only appears when the finance money read is present; no balances item appeared for the desk, so the page that exists to hand the shift over omits the largest open risk. Also the list says 'have not come' at 13:10, before the day has ended.
expected: A hand-over lists everything outstanding the next shift must act on, including overdue guests and what they owe; 'not come yet' until the cut-off.
suggested_fix: Add an overdue-departures item built from the desk section (count, amount, oldest) and reword the arrivals item to 'still expected'.

where: /en/arrivals (2 results) against /en/close-day (13 days waiting, Oct 11 to Oct 23)
observed: Close the day lists 'mahnoor, RJY1FR2, 201, due Oct 11, 2026' as an arrival not checked in, and that one booking is what holds the oldest day open for 13 days. Arrivals shows only two rows (a booking due yesterday and one awaiting confirmation) and not this one. The desk has no work list for a guest who never came; the first place it shows is a month-end screen. Same as FO-02 of 2026-10-22.
expected: Arrivals lists every past-dated booking that is still confirmed, with check in, no-show and cancel in the row.
suggested_fix: Add a 'Still to resolve' group (confirmed bookings whose first night has passed) to Arrivals and to Today's attention list.

where: /en/room-calendar, drag Layla Hassan (107, in house to Oct 28) onto the empty-looking row 306, drop opens Move Guest. Verified as Front desk only. Staging data: booking RMS0CYC, Confirmed, Oct 19 to Oct 21, never arrived.
observed: The dialog opens prefilled 107 to 306 (good), then flags 306 as 'BOOKED . RMS0CYC' with the red message 'Booking RMS0CYC holds some of those nights', and 'Move Guest' stays disabled even after a reason is chosen. The calendar shows 306 empty for the whole 30-day window (the booking ended before the window starts), the dialog says the move is 'from tonight', and today is Oct 24, so the only booking in the way is three days in the past. The desk cannot see why, the message names a code instead of a Guest or dates, and the footer gives no reason for the disabled button once the reason is picked (it only says 'Say why to continue' before). Cause is inferred: the check appears to cover the stay's past nights, not only tonight onward (not checked in code).
expected: A move 'from tonight' is only checked against tonight and later. When a booking does block it, the message names the Guest and dates and the footer says what to fix.
suggested_fix: Check only nights from tonight for an in-house move. Name 'Guest name, Oct 19 to Oct 21, not arrived' in the message and put that same sentence beside the disabled button. Offer 'Mark as no-show' there for a past never-arrived booking (see RC-S5-03 for acting from a bar).

where: /en/configuration, 'Check rooms after cleaning', confirm dialog for 'Save for every Property'
observed: The confirm reads 'This changes Check rooms after cleaning for every Property: from "Off" to "On".' The card above it says a Property follows its Organization unless it has its own answer, so only Properties without their own answer change; here this Property already has its own answer (On) and would not change. The sentence overstates the effect and gives no count, so an Owner of several Properties may believe all of them now inspect. I stopped at the dialog and chose Keep editing; the override rule is read from the card copy and code, not tested.
expected: The consequence says how many Properties change and which keep their own answer.
suggested_fix: 'This changes the default for the Organization. 3 Properties follow it and will change; 1 keeps its own answer (Demo Otel İstanbul).'

where: /en/today and /en/finance?show=owing, en, 1440px, Prizic Demo staging data (30 open folios)
observed: The same question, what do guests owe, has three answers. Today: 'Balance on today's departures TRY 92,160.00' (25 guests) is larger than 'Balance across open folios TRY 66,335.00' (30 folios), so a subset exceeds the whole. Finance, Owing view: '27 folios owe TRY 94,335.00 in all'. I summed the Balance column of those 27 rows and got 66,335.00; the extra 28,000.00 is three 'at check-out' nights (11,200 + 11,200 + 5,600) shown only in small grey sub-lines. Folio 404 reads TRY 11,200.00 on Today and 'TRY 0.00' in the Finance Balance column. The rows that rank first in 'Owing' are the ones whose Balance cell says TRY 0.00.
expected: One word, one definition. A figure called balance means the same number on Today, Departures and Finance, or the label says what is added (for example 'owed now' versus 'owed at check-out').
suggested_fix: Show 'Owed now' and 'Plus nights at check-out' as two labelled numbers in the Finance summary line and on the Today tiles, and use the same split in the Balance column so the sort key is visible. Make the Today departures tile say which departures it counts.

where: /en/analytics (Month, October 2026), en, 1440px; staging data where early-October days have 3 available units and later days 42
observed: Occupancy above 100% is shown as if true. Unit type 'Room' reads 246 available, 261 occupied, 106.1%. Day by day: Oct 11 133.3%, Oct 14 166.7%, Oct 15 366.7%, Oct 17 766.7%, Oct 18 900.0% (27 occupied on 3 available). The headline 88.2% (270 / 306) is built from these rows. Nothing marks the figure as impossible or explains it. Likely cause is available nights counted from when a unit was created (inferred); I did not check the data.
expected: A rate that cannot exceed 100% never appears above 100% without a visible reason. A reader should not have to wonder whether the report or the hotel is wrong.
suggested_fix: Where occupied exceeds available, show a warning badge on that row and on the headline ('more nights occupied than units available: check unit set-up dates'), and link to the place the unit's available-from date is set. Do not silently clamp.

where: /en/hr?tab=payroll, Approve and lock (not reachable on staging: 0 employees)
observed: Approving a payroll run locks it permanently ("no way yet to reverse or revise it", code messages), while the same tab says the social security, income tax and stamp duty figures are placeholders "that must not be used to pay anyone". The owner can lock a run built on figures the product itself calls unapproved. The dialog needs an "I understand" tick, so the click is deliberate, but there is still no way back. I could only see the empty state; the dialog text is read from code.
expected: A run on placeholder deductions is either not lockable, or lockable with a visible way to supersede it.
suggested_fix: Until deductions are approved: disable Approve and lock with the reason, or add a reopen-by-owner path that keeps the history.

where: /en/hr, End employment dialog; /en/people
observed: Ending employment deliberately does not end sign-in access (dialog copy: "Ending employment does not remove their access to the system"). The dialog links to People, which is good, but nothing on either screen shows "left HR, still has access". A leaver keeps signing in until someone remembers to do a second job on a second screen. Read from code; staging has no employees so I could not open the dialog.
expected: The person who ends employment is offered the access removal in the same step, or the People roster flags members whose employment ended.
suggested_fix: Add an "Also remove access in People" option in the End employment dialog (shown only to those holding staff.administer), or a "Left HR on 12 Oct" tag in the People status column.

where: /en/reservations > New reservation > Guest name and Telephone, 1440 px, demo data (43 bookings)
observed: The 'Guests already on file' suggestion exists and works for a name typed with its accents or a surname ('Emre', 'Tanaka' list the guest). It does not fire in two cases a Turkish desk meets daily. (a) 'Ozdemir' typed without the umlaut finds nothing, although the list search above it forgives accents and finds 'Özdemir'. (b) A phone number typed into Telephone ('0537 021 04 95', a guest who exists) produces no suggestion. The dialog's own copy adds that a guest with no email on file 'cannot be matched automatically'. The booking then creates a second Guest record silently.
expected: Suggestions use the same accent-forgiving, digit-normalising matcher as the list search, and also run on the telephone field. Picking one books onto that Guest even when they have no email.
suggested_fix: Reuse the list search normaliser for the suggestion query, add a telephone-triggered lookup (digits only, last 7-10 digits), and match on Guest id (not on email) when a suggestion is picked.

where: /en/reservations (All tab, default sort), demo data
observed: A Confirmed booking whose dates are 13 days past (mahnoor, RJY1FR2, Oct 11 to Oct 12) sits in All with the plain green 'Confirmed' chip, exactly like a future booking. It is the first row because the list sorts oldest start date first. No Check in is offered, no 'late' cue. Overdue in-house guests get a red 'Overdue - N days' chip; a guest who never arrived gets nothing. It is in none of the tabs except All. (Front-office FO-02 reported the same data from Arrivals and the calendar.)
expected: A booking whose arrival date has passed without check-in is flagged ('Did not arrive - 13 days') with its three outcomes in the row, and it is counted somewhere the desk looks.
suggested_fix: Add a 'Late arrival' chip and an 'Unresolved' tab (or include in Arriving today), with No-show / Cancel / Change booking one click away.

where: /en/today, 1440 px, Demo Otel Istanbul, 13:05-13:17 on 2026-10-24; data: 29 in house, 27 due out (22 overdue), 2 arrivals, 42 rooms
observed: 'Expected tonight' is two different numbers depending on the layout of the same page at the same minute. Timeline tile 'In house now 29, 4 expected tonight, of 42 rooms' and Night desk '4 of 42 rooms tonight, 10%' use in-house minus all 27 leaving plus 2 arriving. Next up ('In house 29, 25 expected tonight') and Overview ('Expected tonight 25 / 42 available rooms (60%)') use the server's expectedTonight. A manager reading 10% and another reading 60% on the same evening will plan different nights. The Manager's Night desk contradicts itself on one screen: the headline and waterfall say 'Tonight 4' ('4 of 42 rooms tonight, 10%') while the 'Next seven nights, Rooms held' chart directly beneath shows Saturday (tonight) as 25.
expected: One definition of tonight everywhere (TL-S2-11, TD-S7-01). Either overdue guests count as staying until they are checked out, or they do not, but every layout says the same number and names its rule.
suggested_fix: Compute 'expected tonight' once on the server from the same inputs the desk section uses and feed it to the tile, the Night desk waterfall, Next up and Overview; add one sentence under the figure saying whether overdue guests are counted.

where: /en/departures, sidebar roles, 1200 and 1440 px, 27 in-house rows, one guest name of about 80 characters
observed: The table is 1523 px wide in a 1104 px box at 1440 px (1028 px at 1200). The Guest column is 627 px on every row, so Room, Leaves and Balance sit under the pinned Check out column. To read the balance or the overdue days the desk scrolls sideways, and then the guest name has scrolled away: a red balance with no name beside it. The column width is set by the longest name in the list (table-layout auto, all cells 627 px); the long QA name is the likely cause, which I could not confirm without changing data.
expected: At the usual laptop width the desk sees guest, room, how late and what they owe in one glance, next to the Check out button. A long name wraps or truncates and never pushes the money off screen.
suggested_fix: Cap the Guest column (max width with truncation and a title), keep Leaves and Balance before the pinned action column, and pin the Guest column when the table must scroll.

where: Departures row menu > Change departure, Camila Torres (room 102, leaves today)
observed: 'One more night' is the most common change. The dialog opens with the date field already at the current departure and an error under it, 'That is already the departure.', and the Save button disabled with 'Pick the new departure to continue'. There is no +1 night shortcut. From the list: menu, item, open the picker, pick the date, save is 5 clicks. The stay ruler labels skip days (Oct 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24).
expected: The dialog opens on 'tomorrow' (or offers +1, +2 night chips) and shows no error before the user has done anything.
suggested_fix: Tweak: do not show the 'already the departure' message until the field is touched, and prefill the next day. Proposal: +1 / +2 night chips (RC-DEF-04 family).

where: /en/departures, row menu, Finance, top-chips navigation
observed: The row menu offers Open folio and 'Show on the room map'. The map link goes to /en/rooms, which refuses Finance: 'Your role can't open this page. It needs the permission "Take a booking"'. Finance has no Rooms entry in its navigation, so the app offers a link it then refuses.
expected: A role never sees a menu item it cannot open.
suggested_fix: Hide 'Show on the room map' for roles without the Rooms permission.

where: /en/departures, Finance, 27 in-house rows, 20 overdue with a balance (TRY 53,075.00)
observed: Finance reads this page to chase balances, and every row shows the amount in red. The folio is only reachable from the '...' menu (2 clicks), and the balance is not a link. Sort by Balance is one click and works; the 'Overdue and owing' chip gives the 20-row list and its total.
expected: Click the balance to open that folio.
suggested_fix: Make the balance a link to the Folio for roles that can open Finance.

where: /en/departures at 768 px, keyboard only
observed: Inside the page there are 13 tab stops before the first Check out button (two view links, three chips, the search, Columns, five sort headers, Copy reference). Every further row costs three more stops (Copy reference, Check out, More actions), so the 15th check-out is about 55 key presses. Arrivals uses the same table (the 2026-10-11 count was 9 stops). Check-in moves focus to the next row, which helps; check-out does not.
expected: A skip link to the list or a roving row focus; Check out reachable in one or two stops per row.
suggested_fix: Move focus to the next row's Check out after a check-out; take Copy reference out of the tab order (it is a convenience).

where: /en/room-calendar, overdue bar, drawer, 'Change departure'. Derya Polat, 6 days overdue.
observed: The dialog says 'Pick the day they now leave' but opens with the departure field empty ('Thu, Oct 15 to Open-ended'), so the desk must open the picker and choose a date; Save stays disabled until then. The ruler above shows only Oct 15 to Oct 18, not today (Oct 24), and 'Open-ended' reads like a valid choice. Minimum path for 'one more night' from the bar: click bar, Change departure, open picker, pick day, Save = 5 clicks (verified up to Save; Save not pressed).
expected: The dialog opens prefilled from the gesture: for an overdue Guest, 'leaves today' or 'tomorrow' ready to confirm, with the price consequence shown, so it is 3 clicks.
suggested_fix: Prefill the departure with tomorrow (editable) for an overdue Guest, show chips 'Leaves today / +1 night / +2 nights', extend the ruler to today, and replace the 'Open-ended' placeholder with 'Choose a day'. Keep the price line as the confirm.

where: /en/room-calendar, Move Guest dialog opened by a drop. 12 rooms free tonight on staging.
observed: The room picker lists five rooms by default: 406 Suite FREE, 101 NOT READY, 102 OCCUPIED, 103 OCCUPIED, then the dropped room, with '36 more units. Type to find one'. Two of the five are occupied while 12 rooms are free, so finding a free clean room means typing. Same family as FO-04.
expected: The default list is free and ready rooms first, taken rooms hidden or last, with a one-click 'Free only'.
suggested_fix: Sort by available, then ready, then the rest; collapse OCCUPIED behind 'Show taken rooms'.

where: /en/room-calendar drawers: 'Open in Departures' (overdue) and 'Open in Reservations' (confirmed).
observed: Both links go to the plain list (URL carries only ?property=...), not to this booking, and the overdue drawer tells the desk 'Check them out, or change their departure' while offering no check-out button. The desk must find the Guest again in a list of 29 in-house. Whether the target page highlights the booking is unknown (not checked).
expected: The link opens the page with this booking selected or filtered.
suggested_fix: Pass the reservation id (?reservation=...) and scroll to or open that row; until check-out can be done from the drawer (RC-S5-03, filed), name the link 'Check out in Departures'.

where: /en/rooms (map) at 1280 and 375 px; list view for comparison.
observed: In the map the only clickable part of a tile is the small status pill (guest name, 'Free', 'Reserved'). Pressing a guest's name (Derya Polat) opens 'Block room', not the stay. The list view has an explicit 'Report or block' button, so the same action is clear there and hidden in the map. The pill is 21 px tall at 375 px.
expected: A tile shows what pressing it does, and the guest's name is not a block button; touch targets are at least 44 px.
suggested_fix: Add a visible 'Block / report' control on tile hover and focus, keep the pill as a status, and make its hit area 44 px on touch.

where: /en/rooms, Add rooms dialog as Manager, 1280x860 and 768x878. First number 301, number of rooms 3 (301 to 303 already exist).
observed: The new preview ('Adds 3 rooms: 301 to 303, sleeps 2') exists but sits below the visible area: its bottom (849 px) is under the dialog's footer (dialog ends at 844 px), so it is not seen unless the form is scrolled; the screenshot shows only the button 'Add 3 rooms'. The preview does not warn that 301, 302 and 303 already exist, and the button stays enabled, so the refusal can only come after pressing it (inferred; not pressed). Forty rooms ('Add 40 rooms: 501 to 540') are also one press, with no undo (RB-S3-12 deferred).
expected: The preview is next to the button, flags existing numbers before the press, and a large count asks once.
suggested_fix: Move the preview into the sticky footer above the button; check the numbers against the room list client-side and say 'Already in use: 301, 302, 303'; above 20 rooms show 'Add 40 rooms?' with the first and last number.

where: /en/room-calendar, 1280x860, default view.
observed: The grid header starts about 371 px down (2-line description, toolbar row, filter row, checkbox row, legend line) so only ten rooms (103 to 112) are visible on a laptop-height screen. The 2026-10-11 measure was about 330 px; this is not better. The grid header is sticky, which helps once scrolled.
expected: The grid starts within about 250 px at 1280x860, with filters one click away.
suggested_fix: Fold the two filter rows and the legend into the same disclosure the phone already uses ('Filters'), keep the description to one line.

where: /en/branding at 375 px
observed: On a phone the Preview card is below the Logo card, about 1,000 px under the colour field, so typing a colour shows only a 24 px swatch in view; the buttons and header that show the result are two screens down. The page is 1,371 px tall at 375, no horizontal scroll (verified by scrollWidth 375).
expected: The result of the edit is in view while editing.
suggested_fix: On narrow screens put the Preview directly under the colour field, or keep it sticky at the top while the form scrolls.

where: /en/integrations?property=..., Owner and Manager, 1440 px, Demo Otel İstanbul
observed: The page says 'This module isn't switched on at this Property. Your Organization has it, but this Property doesn't. Choose another Property from the menu at the top, or ask your Organization's Owner to request it for this Property.' Read by the Owner, it tells them to ask the Owner. There is no Property menu at the top: the header shows the Property name as plain text, and the Organization has one Property. There is no request button, no switch in Configuration (deferred, CF-DEF-02), and Integrations is absent from both roles' sidebars, so this page is only reachable by typing the URL. The two roles have a dead end with advice that does not apply.
expected: The message matches who is reading and ends in something that can be done.
suggested_fix: For an Owner: 'Integrations is not switched on at Demo Otel İstanbul. It is switched on from the Control Plane (Prizic).' with the contact route; for a Manager name the Owner. Do not mention a Property menu unless the viewer has more than one Property.

where: /en/integrations (not reachable on staging; read from features/integrations/components/integrations-view.tsx)
observed: Page order is four stat tiles (all zero for a new setup), then the failures list, then the endpoints section, and the 'Add endpoint' button sits in that last section's header. For a first-time setup the one action the page exists for is below tiles of zeros and an empty failures table. The module is switched off at the demo Property so I could not render it; this is read from code only.
expected: Zero endpoints: the page leads with the empty state and its Add endpoint action.
suggested_fix: When there are no endpoints, show the endpoints empty state first and hide the failure tiles until there is something to fail. With endpoints, put failures above (as now).

where: /en/configuration, Manager view, 1440 px
observed: Read-only settings give the reason in two wordings for one state: 'Only someone who reaches every Property can rename the Organization.' and 'Changing the default needs access to every Property.', plus 'Only someone who reaches every Property can change the Organization's setting.' None names a role, so the Manager does not know who to ask. 'Reaches' is the product's internal word.
expected: One sentence for one state, naming the role that can.
suggested_fix: 'Only an Owner can change this because it applies to every Property.' used everywhere on the page.

where: /en/audit-log?record=<id>, 1440 px, a Folio payment record and a check-out record
observed: The record detail table still shows raw keys: a Checked out record lists "nightsCharged" next to words like "Folio closed" and "Balance at closing" (a bare 0, no currency); the payment record lists "Line 6c80f7c9", a truncated id nobody can look up. Read as text on the live page; the screenshot shows the Line id.
expected: Every row of the details table is a plain-language label with a value I can act on, money with its currency, and ids replaced by names or a link.
suggested_fix: Give the remaining keys a label, give 'Balance at closing' the Property currency, and replace the Line id by a link to the Folio line or drop it.

where: /en/audit-log and ?record=<id>, English and Arabic, payment records
observed: A posted payment shows as "Payment · -TRY 2,735.00" (Arabic "-2,735.00 TRY"), with a minus sign, in the list and in the detail table. To a hotel owner a minus beside a payment reads as a refund. Which sign convention the ledger uses is inferred: the screen never explains it.
expected: A payment posted reads as money received ("TRY 2,735.00"); a refund or reversal is the one that carries a sign or the word 'refund'.
suggested_fix: Show the absolute amount for a payment and keep the sign only where it tells payment from refund; or say 'credit to the Folio' beside it.

where: /en/data-export, History, a ready export requested by someone else
observed: From the code: every ready row shows a Download button to everyone who can read the list, but the download re-asks the downloader's permissions. A Finance user who sees a colleague's ready Guests export and clicks Download is sent back with the banner 'That file is no longer available. Files are kept for 7 days, and a download also needs your role to still cover the data in it'. The file is not gone; the sentence names two causes and the viewer cannot tell which. There were no exports on staging to click, so this is read from recent-exports-table.tsx and the download route, not seen.
expected: A row I cannot download shows why before I click, or no button.
suggested_fix: Compare the dataset list to the viewer's abilities (already on the page as 'abilities') and show 'Your role cannot download this' in place of the button; keep the redirect banner for real expiry.

where: /en/data-export, Request an export, Dates
observed: The date range note says which clock the days are read on only when Audit log is ticked ("Days are read on the clock of Europe/Istanbul", visible in the Arabic screenshot). For Folios and Reservations the form says nothing, and the file note says "times are UTC". A Finance user cutting 'last month' of payments cannot tell whether a payment at 00:30 Istanbul time on the 1st falls in the month, nor why the time in the file differs by three hours from the screen. Which clock the folio cut uses is unknown to me; the missing sentence is verified (code: ranged && chosen.includes('audit_log')).
expected: The form states the clock for every dataset it cuts.
suggested_fix: Show the 'days are read on the clock of ...' line whenever a range is set and any ranged dataset is ticked, and state the timezone offset in the CSV note.

where: /en/finance?show=owing -> open a folio -> Back, en, 1440px
observed: Opening a folio from the Owing list drops the filter: after the click the address is ?folio=... only, and the Back arrow links to /en/finance?property=... (all folios, page 1). Search text, page number and the Owing chip are lost. Typing in the search box also leaves the address unchanged, so a refresh loses it. Collecting from ten debtors in a row means re-choosing Owing ten times.
expected: Back returns to the list exactly as it was left.
suggested_fix: Carry show, page, per-page and the search text in the address, and make Back and 'close folio' return to that address.

where: All Finance-role pages, 375px wide
observed: The six page chips (Today, Departures, Maintenance, Finance, Analytics, Data export) sit in a row that is wider than the screen: at 375px only Today, Departures and Maintenance show, with no scroll cue. The chip for the page you are on (Finance, Analytics) is off-screen. Going from Finance to Analytics on a phone means finding the hidden part of the strip.
expected: On a phone the current page is visible and the other pages are reachable without guessing.
suggested_fix: Scroll the active chip into view on load and show an edge fade, or collapse the strip to a menu under 480px.

where: Folio of Derya Polat 103 (booking has no price), en; Record payment dialog
observed: The folio says: 'This booking has no price, so no nights are charged to this folio. Add a price to the booking from the Reservations screen.' A Finance user cannot open Reservations: /en/reservations answers 'Your role can't open this page. It needs the permission Take a booking.' The booking reference is plain text for Finance, while the Owner sees it as a link. The same folio's payment dialog says 'This Guest owes TRY 7,330.00 now, counting the nights check-out will still charge' although the folio just said no nights are charged. The guest is also 6 days overdue, so the bill may be understated and nobody on this page can fix it.
expected: A message that tells you to go somewhere only appears when you can go there; otherwise it names who can act.
suggested_fix: For roles without the booking permission say 'Ask the front desk or a manager to add a price to booking RQQV7RJ'. Drop the 'check-out will still charge' clause when no nights are being charged.

where: /en/analytics?month=2026-10&day=2026-10-05 (day drawer), en, 1440px
observed: The drawer lists stay 102 with 'No price on the booking' and nothing to open: the only links in the drawer are previous and next day. The page text above tells the reader to 'open a booking to add its price', but there is no link to the booking or its folio, and 'Nights with no charge' has no action.
expected: From a stay in the drawer I can open its booking (if my role may) or its folio.
suggested_fix: Make each stay row a link to the booking for roles with the booking permission, and to the folio otherwise.

where: /en/housekeeping and /en/maintenance, 768 px wide, chips navigation, 4 and 6 chips
observed: At 768 px the page-bar chips live in a 301 px strip (scrollWidth 558 for Housekeeping) even though the bar has spare room around it. The active chip shows only its icon: the label 'Housekeeping' is cut off and 'Maintenance' is off screen. For Finance (six chips) Maintenance is cut ('Maint') and Finance, Analytics and Data export are past the right edge (last chip ends at x=859 on a 768 screen). Nothing but a clipped word hints that the strip scrolls. At 375 px the same strip clips the active label ('Housel').
expected: The role can read the name of the page it is on and see every page it has, or sees an explicit scroll cue. A role with six pages or fewer should not need to swipe a 301 px strip on a tablet.
suggested_fix: Give the chips the free width of the bar (let the property name and flag wrap or move below at <1024 px), keep the active chip fully labelled and scrolled into view, and add an edge fade as a scroll cue.

where: /en/housekeeping, 375 px, after ticking one room
observed: Ticking the first room inserts the bulk bar above the table and pushes the list down: the first row moved from y=595 to y=817 (222 px) in the same tap, so the next room to tick is no longer where the finger was. While scrolling, the bar stays at the top (sticky, as HK-S3-14 asks) but it is 210 px tall, 26% of an 812 px phone, in three rows (count, Mark clean/inspected, Mark dirty, Clear selection). Mark clean and Mark inspected sit side by side with Mark dirty on a second line.
expected: Selecting rooms does not move the rooms; the bar is one compact row so most of the phone shows rooms.
suggested_fix: Render the bar as a fixed one-row strip at the bottom (or top) overlaying the list, with icon buttons and a count; reserve its height so the list never jumps.

where: /en/housekeeping, 375 px
observed: The five stat tiles wrap onto three rows (about 340 px of 812). Search, status chips and Floor follow, and the first room starts at y=595 of 812. The tile counts repeat the Clean, Inspected and Dirty chips directly below them, and the tiles are not controls.
expected: The first room is on the first screen and the counts are also the filters.
suggested_fix: On phones show the counts once, as the filter chips, and drop or collapse the tiles (Ready to let can sit beside the page title).

where: Maintenance request drawer and the two report dialogs, 375 px and 768 px
observed: The illustrated header takes 350 to 400 px. In the request drawer the title, which is the only thing that says which request this is, is cut mid-word behind the wrench: 'Windo / w will / not...' at 375 px (MT-7) and 'Air conditioni' at 768 px (MT-1). In the 'Report a problem' and 'What does the guest need?' dialogs the header plus the intro paragraph fill 55% of the phone before the first field, and How urgent and Take it out of order are below the fold.
expected: The title is readable in full (wrapping), and on a phone the first field is on the first screen.
suggested_fix: Let the masthead title wrap and grow (or use a plain heading on narrow screens), and drop the illustration and intro text below 640 px.

where: Page bar and sidebar, all three pages
observed: No page shows how many requests are waiting: the chips (Housekeeping, Finance) and the sidebar (Front desk, Manager, Owner) carry no count for Guest Experience or Maintenance (Guest Experience has 6 open, Maintenance 6 open and 3 urgent when read). The report dialog says honestly 'Nobody is notified: the request appears on this board', so the only way to learn about a fault or a guest is to open the page. The dialog's own words make this a missing signal, not an oversight, but it is the friction that matters most on a floor.
expected: A role sees at a glance that something is waiting.
suggested_fix: Show the open count on the Guest Experience and Maintenance entries (urgent in the danger tone). Notifications themselves are deferred (MT-DEF-15).

where: /en/people > change role > confirm dialog (Housekeeping to Manager), 1440px
observed: The confirm names the consequence (every session ends) and what is gained, which fixes the old PEOPLE-10. But "They gain" is one unbroken 25-item run-on sentence in catalogue order. "Define and edit roles", "Manage staff records and payroll" and "Reverse a payment" sit mid-sentence with "Keep the equipment register". Terms like "Folio" are unexplained, and the heading breaks the email mid-word ("housekeeping@p / rizic.com").
expected: The owner can see at a glance whether the change hands over money, people or payroll powers.
suggested_fix: Group the gained and lost lists under the six section headings the role grid already uses (Front desk, Money, People and HR...), put money and people items first, and let the email heading wrap at "@".

where: /en/hr, Register employee / Edit employee dialogs
observed: The Start date field has max = today in both dialogs (register-employee-dialog.tsx, edit-employee-dialog.tsx). A seasonal or new hire starting next Monday cannot be registered on Friday, so they are missing from next week's rota and leave screens until the day they start.
expected: The owner can register a hire with a future start date; the person appears on the rota from that date.
suggested_fix: Allow future start dates; show "Starts Mon 2 Nov" on the card and keep them out of payroll for earlier periods.

where: /en/hr?tab=employees, 1440px, 0 employees, 5 sign-ins without a record
observed: The first-time page stacks two empty states: "Staff without an employment record" (one "Register as employee" button per sign-in, which links the login) and below it "No employees registered" with a separate "Add employee" button (which creates a record without a login). A first-time owner cannot tell which to use; whether Add employee for somebody who already has a sign-in creates an unlinked duplicate I could not determine. Registering the five sign-ins is five separate dialogs.
expected: One empty state with one primary action, and a clear statement of which option links a login.
suggested_fix: Keep the sign-in list as the main action when sign-ins exist; hide the second empty card in that case. Consider "Register all five" later.

where: /en/hr at 375px
observed: The page no longer scrolls sideways (document width 375), but the four-tab bar is 422 px wide inside a 351 px scroll container: the Payroll tab, the most consequential one, shows only its icon and is cut off, with a thin scrollbar as the only cue. Tab right edges measured at 169, 247, 333 and 425 px.
expected: All four tabs are visible or an obvious scroll cue is shown; the tab bar fits at 375 px.
suggested_fix: Drop the icons and the count below 400 px, or let the tabs shrink to fit; or fade the right edge.

where: Workspace rail, /en/food-and-beverage and /en/inventory, Demo Otel Istanbul; 1280 px sidebar and 375 px bottom bar; Owner and Manager
observed: Food and Beverage and Inventory are first-class rail entries between live pages (Maintenance, Food and Beverage, Inventory, Finance). Each opens a page with nothing to do. On a phone the bottom bar holds 14 entries and scrolls sideways; the two placeholders are entries 6 and 7 and push Finance to 8th. The registry says built:false for both; ADR 0056 offers them to any role holding configuration.manage on purpose.
expected: A destination that cannot be used yet takes no place in the daily navigation. The people who press it 20 times a day (Finance, Analytics, Configuration) should not scroll past two dead entries.
suggested_fix: Filter built:false screens out of useWorkspaceNav (keep the routes so a bookmark still lands on the placeholder). If the owner wants them discoverable, list them once on Configuration under 'Coming modules'. This reverses a line of ADR 0056, so it needs the owner's yes.

where: /en/food-and-beverage, /en/inventory, /tr, /ar; desktop and 375 px; placeholder card
observed: The card reads like a feature description: 'Meal plans, outlets and consumption records.' / 'Stock movements, counts and procurement.' The only sign that it is not available is a small uppercase 'PLANNED' label above it. Nothing says 'you cannot use this yet', what has to exist first (the handover table says Food and Beverage needs Inventory and a Folio to charge to; Inventory needs a platform stock module) or what to do in the meantime. No button leads anywhere useful; the only action is a link that leaves the app.
expected: First sentence says it is not available yet. A second line names what must exist first in plain words. One action that leaves the person somewhere useful (back to Today, or the page that does the nearest job today, for example Maintenance for equipment).
suggested_fix: Reword screenSummary.* in the three locales to 'Not available yet. Meal plans and outlets will arrive after Inventory and Billing are in use.' Add a primary button 'Back to Today'. Keep PLANNED as the label.

where: https://ranza.46-225-168-54.nip.io/en/sign-in (Workspace sign-in), signed out
observed: The Workspace sign-in has no 'Forgot your password?' link and no line saying who can help. The Portal sign-in has both. A staff member locked out before a shift has no on-screen next step. Verified in the accessibility tree and by the absence of any reset or help route in the workspace app (only sign-in and accept-invitation exist).
expected: The same help line the Portal has: 'Can't sign in? Ask your Property's administrator.' Naming who resets a password is possible without email delivery.
suggested_fix: Add one muted line under the Sign in button in the three locales; no new route needed.

where: /en/reservations > New reservation, after choosing unit 104, 1440 x 900 viewport
observed: The price answer ('TRY 2,800.00 a night - 2 nights: TRY 5,600.00 in total') appears only after a unit is picked, and it renders below the visible part of the dialog (the dialog body scrolls; the line is under the footer until you scroll). The dates field shows 'Wed, Oct 28 -> Fri, Oct 30' with no night count. The total, which is the thing the guest is waiting for, is the one thing not in view when the Create button lights up.
expected: Night count beside the dates the moment both are chosen; price and total pinned next to the Create button or at the top of the unit section.
suggested_fix: Move the price line into the sticky footer next to Create ('2 nights - TRY 5,600'), and print the night count inside the date field.

where: /en/reservations, keyboard only: row '...' menu > Mark as no-show / Change booking / Change departure, then Escape
observed: After a row-action dialog closes, document.activeElement is BODY, not the row's '...' button. The New reservation dialog does return focus to its button. A keyboard user doing the 20th amendment of the day starts again from the top of the page every time. (Menu open and item selection by keyboard work: Enter opens the menu, arrows move, Enter selects.)
expected: Focus returns to the row's actions button (or the row) when its dialog closes.
suggested_fix: Restore focus to the row trigger on close; keep a stable row key so the trigger survives the re-render.

where: /en/reservations > row '...' > Change booking on a Confirmed booking whose dates are in the past (mahnoor, Oct 11 to Oct 12, Suite 201)
observed: The dialog opens with the past dates and a red 'The arrival must be today or later.' already showing; Save is disabled. Nothing says that the guest never arrived or that Mark as no-show or Cancel is the right action. The desk member has to work out for themselves why the form is in error.
expected: Opening Change booking on a booking that is already late says so in plain words and offers the two real outcomes (move it, or mark it a no-show) before showing an error.
suggested_fix: When arrival < today and status is Confirmed, replace the red line with 'This booking was due on Oct 11 and the Guest has not arrived' plus 'Mark as no-show' and 'Pick new dates'.

where: /en/reservations > tab Arriving today > Oliver Smith, Requested, due today
observed: The row's action cell reads 'The booking has to be confirmed first.' The row menu offers only Show on the room map, Change booking and Cancel booking. There is no Confirm action anywhere, so the instruction points at a step the desk cannot take. (Confirming a requested booking is a deferred row, RG-DEF-03, so this is a dead-end message on data that exists on staging, not a missing feature report.)
expected: Either the row offers Confirm, or the message says what the desk can do now ('Change it to confirmed through Change booking' or 'Ask a Manager').
suggested_fix: Short term: reword to name the available action. Long term: build RG-DEF-03.

where: /en/reservations tabs and search, demo data (at least 8 overdue stays)
observed: The tab 'Departing today 27' contains guests who were due days ago (8 of the first 10 rows are 'Overdue - 1 to 6 days'), so the label and the count are wrong for what is in it. Typing 'overdue' in the search finds 0 rows although the word is on 8+ rows. There is no Overdue tab, so the desk cannot get a list of 'guests who should have gone'.
expected: A tab or filter named for the thing: 'Overdue'. 'Departing today' counts only today. The word on the chip is searchable.
suggested_fix: Add an Overdue tab (red count), restrict Departing today to today, and index the chip text in the search.

where: /en/reservations on open, default tab All, sort by start date ascending
observed: The page opens on All with the oldest bookings first, so the first screen is the Oct 11 never-arrived booking and eight overdue stays; the 2 guests arriving today are one tab away. The tab you chose is not remembered next visit. Per page is 10 of 43.
expected: The screen opens on what the desk does most (arriving today) or on the tab last used, and keeps the page size.
suggested_fix: Remember the last tab and page size per user; sort All by relevance (today first) rather than oldest first.

where: any workspace route, /en, 1440x878 desktop, Owner with 15 rail entries
observed: The expanded sidebar scrolls inside itself. At 1440x878 the last entry (Audit log) sits at y=916, below the fold, and the SYSTEM heading is the last thing visible: Configuration, Branding, Data export and Audit log are hidden. The scrollbar is thin and there is no fade or cue. At 1200x833 the rail is icon-only and also scrolls (content 891 px in a 628 px box).
expected: Every page the role is offered is visible, or the rail says plainly that more is below.
suggested_fix: Tighten row height and section spacing so 15 entries fit at 878 px, pin SYSTEM entries beside the account card, or add a bottom fade and scroll cue.

where: any unknown path, for example /en/nonexistent-page, /en/front-office, /today (no locale), /en/reservations/123; en, tr and ar
observed: Unknown addresses show the framework's bare default: "404 | This page could not be found.", in English, on white, with no Ranza shell, no link and no button. In /ar and /tr it is still English and left-to-right. /en/front-office, the name of a rail group, is a 404. A bookmark or typed address that is slightly wrong ends here. The page has no back control either (ADR 0035).
expected: A branded page in the person's language with the shell or at least a Go to Today button.
suggested_fix: Add a localized not-found page inside the locale layout with a Go to Today button; make /en/front-office open Front Office's first page; send locale-less paths to the remembered locale.

where: any page the role is refused, for example Housekeeping on /en/finance, Front desk on /en/people, Manager on /en/branding; en, tr, ar
observed: The refusal "Your role can't open this page" has no button. The text names a permission in system words (Housekeeping sees "Open and close a Folio (a guest's bill)") and says to ask someone who manages staff, "Owners and Managers can". A Manager refused Branding is told Managers can add it, and cannot tell if they can add it to themselves. It never says which person at this hotel to ask or what to do meanwhile. The back arrow and chips are present, so the person is not trapped, but nothing is offered.
expected: A Go to Today button, the page's purpose in a few words, and who to ask by role.
suggested_fix: Add the Go to Today action already used for not-reachable; say "Ask your Owner" when the Organization has one Owner; describe the page, not the permission key.

where: /en/today, desktop sidebar
observed: Front Office is a closed group on Today. Reservations, Room calendar, Arrivals and Departures, the desk's most frequent pages, cost two clicks from Today (open the group, then the page), every shift, every time. The group opens by itself only on its own pages, so the state is not remembered after a reload on Today (verified: aria-expanded false after reload).
expected: A role whose daily work is Front Office sees those pages open.
suggested_fix: Open Front Office by default for roles that hold front desk commands, or remember the last state per device.

where: /en/sign-in after a wrong password
observed: The message is now "That email and password did not match. Check both and try again. Forgotten your password? Contact Prizic support." It names a next step but gives no address, phone or link, and there is no reset flow. A receptionist locked out at the start of a shift cannot act on it. It does not say which of the two was wrong, which is right.
expected: A way to act: a support address or number, or a reset link.
suggested_fix: Add a mailto or phone link, or say who inside the hotel (Owner or Manager) can reset it.

where: /en/today, Overview vs Timeline, 1440 px; 22 overdue departures
observed: 'Checked out' has two denominators. Timeline: '0 / 27, 22 departures overdue'. Overview, same minute: '0 / 5 Checked out, 22 to leave, longest overdue 6 days'. By the numbers, the five is guests due today only and the 27 adds the 22 overdue (inferred from the counts, not from code). The first reads as 'I have 27 to do', the second as 'I have 5, plus a warning'.
expected: One 'checked out of how many' per page, with overdue shown as a separate number.
suggested_fix: Use the same denominator in every layout (due today plus overdue) and keep the overdue count as the sub-line in both.

where: /en/today as Housekeeping, 1440 px, 'Clean these first' (11 rooms) and the 'Dirty 17 to clean' tile
observed: The first screen says '17 to clean' but the list that follows is 11 rooms, and the second to fourth rows (102, 112, 206) are rooms with a guest still in them: 'A Guest is still in it; it is cleaned once they leave', no action. Rooms 304 and 307, which can be cleaned now (Mark clean), sit below them. Three of the first six rows are not work the housekeeper can do.
expected: The list opens with rooms that can be cleaned now; rooms waiting on a departure sit under a 'Not yet' group; the tile counts what can be cleaned.

where: /en/today Timeline plan, row 24 (Oliver Smith, 402) versus Overview attention card

The Overview card for the same guest says 'Can't check in: The booking is not confirmed yet.' and opens Arrivals. The real blocker is the booking, which Housekeeping cannot fix; the Timeline hides the reason and sends the desk to the wrong page. The House map shows the same 'Check-in blocked' badge without a reason.
expected: The reason, in words, and the page that fixes it.
suggested_fix: Use the Overview card's reason text in the plan, the House map and Next up, and route a booking blocker to Arrivals, a room blocker to Housekeeping.

where: Check out dialog opened from Today for Derya Polat (room 103, 6 days overdue)

The amount at the bottom (TRY 7,330) matches neither sentence unambiguously. The dialog header says 'UNIT 103' while the page behind it says rooms.
expected: The dialog names the money consequence of this guest only: either 'no nights will be charged' or 'N nights, TRY X, will be added'.

where: /en/departures at 768 px, Owner (also true at 1440 with the long name, see ARRIVALS-01)

where: /en/arrivals at 375 and 768 px, Owner, 2 arrivals (one dirty room)

where: /en/arrivals, row Oliver Smith (R758MVJ, room 402), status Awaiting confirmation

where: /en/arrivals and /en/departures rows
observed: The guest name is plain text. The Arrivals menu offers Show on the room map, Open in Housekeeping, Change booking, Mark as no-show, Cancel booking; Departures offers Open folio, Show on the room map, Change departure, Move Guest. expected: Click the guest to see the booking: balance, paid, requests, notes, and the next action.

where: /en/close-day, 13 days waiting
observed: Only the oldest day can be closed ('Close only Sunday, October 11, 2026'), each close with its own reason; clearing 13 days is 13 dialogs (inferred from the single-day dialog; I did not submit). 'What holds each day' reads '1 item open' for seven days and 'and 6 more days' without saying what holds them; only the oldest day is itemised in the dialog, which does now name the guest and room. The word 'only' implies an alternative that is not there.
expected: Close all days through a chosen date with one shared reason, each day itemised.
suggested_fix: Propose a 'Close all days through Oct 23' action with one reason; name the item on each day line; drop 'only'.

where: /en/room-calendar 'Free' row under Sat Oct 24 versus /en/rooms stat tile, same minute.
observed: Calendar says Free 17 for tonight, Rooms says '12 FREE TONIGHT' (and 1 'reserved tonight', 29 'occupied'). The calendar then jumps to Free 40 for Sun Oct 25 although at least 22 overdue guests are still drawn in their rooms until that day's midday. Neither number says what it counts. Same family as FO-03 in the 2026-10-22 report.
expected: One defined number for 'can I sell this tonight' with a label, and a future count that either includes guests still overdue or says it assumes they leave.
suggested_fix: Define 'free tonight' once (vacant tonight, not blocked); label the calendar row 'Free rooms' with a tooltip, and count overdue stays as held until the day they are resolved. Rooms uses the same function.

where: /en/rooms map and list. The only link in the page body is 'Which are clean or dirty? See Housekeeping'.
observed: From a room tile or list row there is no way to the Guest's reservation, the Guest's departure, or the room's row on the calendar. Departures has 'Show on the room map', but the reverse does not exist. The list shows the Guest's name as plain text.
expected: A tile with a Guest opens that stay's details or links to the reservation; a free tile links to the calendar row for that room.
suggested_fix: Make the Guest name a link to the reservation and add 'See on calendar' per room. A new interaction, so proposed only.

where: /en/rooms map and list, staging with 42 rooms.
observed: The page says which rooms are free, reserved, in house, blocked, but not which are clean or dirty; the only help is the line 'Which are clean or dirty? See Housekeeping', which is a working link. The desk still needs two screens to answer 'can I give this room to the Guest now'. Same as FO-05 of the 2026-10-22 report; ROOMS-08 of 2026-10-11 is only partly addressed.
expected: Each free tile shows ready or dirty.
suggested_fix: Add a small readiness mark to each tile and a 'Ready' filter chip.

where: /en/branding; real Portal header from apps/guest-portal layout.tsx and portal-rail.tsx
observed: The Preview card draws a white header with the logo where Ranza's mark would be, titled 'Portal header', plus a button, a link and an 'active item'. In the real Portal (code) the desktop rail keeps Ranza's mark hard-coded (portal-rail.tsx passes BrandMark), the logo appears in the page bar beside the back arrow and breadcrumb, and the bar title reads 'Stay'. The preview therefore shows a logo placement guests never see, no hotel name, and nothing of the rail. The screen also never says where or how to see the real result: no link to the Portal, no note that guests see a change on their next page load.
expected: The preview matches what a guest sees, and the screen says where the brand appears and where it does not.
suggested_fix: Draw the preview as the real page bar (back arrow, logo, 'Stay') beside a rail with the active item, label it with where the logo shows, and add one line: 'Guests see this the next time they open the Portal. The sign-in page stays Ranza's.' (BR-S1-23, BR-S1-28 already decide both facts.)

where: /en/audit-log at 375 px, English, 50 rows
observed: At 375 px only When and What fit. The When column takes about half the width for a full date ("Oct 23, 2026, 23:53"); Where, Who and Why sit behind a sideways scroll (table 923 px in a 341 px wrapper). Who is repeated under the title, which helps, but the Why column, the one a manager opening a correction on a phone wants, is two swipes away. The filters are folded behind a 'Filters' button with a count, which works.
expected: On a phone each record is a card: what, when (short), who, and the reason if there is one.
suggested_fix: Below 640 px render each record as a stacked card, drop the year from the time when it is this year, and show the reason line when present.

where: /en/finance and folio, 375px wide, en
observed: The Balance column, the figure the page exists for, is at x 607-693 inside a 343px scroll box on a 375px screen, so each card shows the name, dates and status and no amount until the person swipes sideways; the Balance sort header is also off-screen. In the folio the line table clips Amount and the Reverse button ('TF' of 'TRY' is all that shows), so a wrong charge cannot be reversed from a phone without discovering a sideways swipe. Nothing hints at the swipe.
expected: At 375px a folio card shows the balance and a folio line shows its amount and Reverse.
suggested_fix: Below 640px render the list cards and folio lines as stacked blocks (name over amount, Reverse as a full-width row action), as Analytics already does for its tables.

where: /en/finance -> folio -> Record payment, en
observed: Taking a payment at the desk, the most frequent finance job for Front desk, costs four clicks from the Finance list: open the row, Record payment, choose method, Record. The amount is prefilled and the method is deliberately not defaulted, which is right. The list rows carry no payment action even though the Owing view tells the clerk exactly who owes.
expected: The common action happens on the row.
suggested_fix: Proposal: a 'Record payment' button on each Owing row that opens the existing dialog prefilled from that row, saving the folio page hop (4 clicks to 3, and no page load). Mews and Cloudbeds put payment on the reservation row.

where: /en/housekeeping, 375 px, 42 rooms, 17 dirty
observed: The repeated action, marking a room clean, is the room's three-dot menu then 'Mark clean': two taps per room, so 80 rooms is 160 taps, each followed by locating the next room. The status chip on the card is not a control. After a mark the result line clears itself in 6 s and has no Undo (code: housekeeping-board.tsx, CONFIRMATION_MS); a wrong-room mark is undone by finding the room again and marking it back (HK-S2-05 says exactly that). Not submitted: stopped at the open menu, nothing persisted.
expected: The common action happens on the thing itself: one tap on the room's status (or a swipe) advances Dirty to Clean, and the confirmation carries a one-tap Undo for the few seconds it is on screen.
suggested_fix: Make the status chip a one-tap 'next status' control with the 6 s confirmation offering Undo; keep the menu for the rarer jumps (Inspected, Dirty). Comparable: Mews and Opera housekeeping task lists, Optii.

where: /en/housekeeping, 375 px
observed: The table is 940 px wide inside a 343 px container (scrollable 597 px). The first screen of each row shows room, status, floor and today's movement, which is a real improvement, but Occupancy ('Guest in house' or 'Vacant', the thing that says whether to knock) and Last changed are reachable only by swiping sideways, and after the swipe the room number has scrolled away so a row reads 'Clean / Guest in house' with no room. The 'Guest in house' chip is cut under the sticky actions column. Nothing says there is more to the right.
expected: On a phone each room is a card that shows number, status, today's movement and occupancy together, with no sideways scroll.
suggested_fix: Below 640 px render rows as stacked cards (room, status chip, today chip, occupancy chip on the first screen), drop Last changed to the card's menu.

where: /en/housekeeping to /en/maintenance?report= and back, 375 px
observed: The Dirty chip and the Floor filter are page state: the address stays /housekeeping?property=... after applying both, so a reload or a trip away resets to 42 rooms. 'Report a problem' navigates to Maintenance; the Back arrow there goes to Today (href /today, seen for Finance, the same page bar), so a housekeeper who reports a fault while working 'Dirty, floor 3' lands on the Today page and must tap the Housekeeping chip and re-apply both filters.
expected: After reporting a fault the way back is the board exactly as left.
suggested_fix: Keep the filters in the address (?status=dirty&floor=3), and when Maintenance is opened from a room send Back to the Housekeeping board with those filters (ADR 0035 allows a link one level up: the origin page).

where: /en/housekeeping and /en/today, staging, shared load
observed: Fetching the page HTML as the signed-in user three times each: Housekeeping 2.5, 2.4, 2.0 s; Today 2.5, 2.2, 2.1 s; Maintenance 0.28, 0.27, 0.29 s; Guest Experience 0.28, 0.25, 0.24 s. A full navigation to the board reports responseEnd 2.4 s (Owner 2.7 s). Other audit agents were loading staging at the same time, so absolute values are inflated, but the eightfold gap was stable. The slow-board fix (PR #97) is not on staging, so this is the expected baseline. Whether each mark then re-renders the board for about this long is inferred from the form action (server action followed by a fresh board), not timed because marking is forbidden here.
expected: The board opens in under a second and a mark confirms immediately.
suggested_fix: Ship PR #97; measure again with the 42 rooms after it lands; return the changed rows from the mark action instead of re-reading the board.

where: /en/maintenance and /en/guest-experience as Housekeeping, 375 px
observed: The Housekeeping account is the assignee of MT-7, MT-2, MT-4, MT-5 and of guest requests #5 and #2 (demo data), yet it sees no Start, Done or Resolve control: Maintenance says 'Moving, assigning and cancelling them needs the permission to manage maintenance', Guest Experience says the same for guest requests. Migration 20260916009900 grants manage_requests only to owner, manager and front desk. Front desk can move guest requests but not maintenance requests. So whoever does the work must phone someone who may press Done. Whether real assignments to housekeeping staff will exist is unknown (they exist only as seeded data here); the shipped roles make the gap structural.
expected: The person a request is assigned to can start it and mark it done, and sees their own list first.
suggested_fix: Add an 'assigned to me' default view and let an assignee (not only a manager) move their own request through In progress and Done; keep assign, priority and cancel with manage. New behaviour, so a proposal for Seif's approval.

where: /en/housekeeping, 375 px and desktop, rooms 108 and 209
observed: A room row never says that a guest request or a fault is open for it. Room 108 has an open 'Room not cleaned today' request (#5, category Housekeeping, In Progress) and 209 holds fault MT-7 (window will not close); on the board both rows read only Dirty / Guest in house, so the housekeeper learns about them only by opening two other pages.
expected: A room with an open request or fault shows a small marker with the count, and the row menu opens it.
suggested_fix: Add a 'Requests' chip on the room row (guest requests and faults for that Unit) linking to the filtered page. A new interaction: proposal.

where: /en/people > Define a role dialog, 1440px, no Organization-authored roles yet
observed: The role editor is a 1,815 px scroll (viewport 846 px) of 32 plain checkboxes in six sections. Nothing summarises the choice: no count of ticked permissions (picking "Start from Front desk" ticks 13 and says so nowhere), no list of the pages the role will open or whether its holder gets a sidebar or top chips (ADR 0056), no flag on the dangerous keys (define roles, manage payroll, post or reverse payments), and no search. Save stays enabled with a name and zero permissions (code: only the name gates the button), which creates a role that reaches only Today. Escape discards all ticks without asking.
expected: Before saving, the owner can read one line that says what the role will be able to do and which pages it opens, and is warned when it holds nothing or holds a high-impact key.
suggested_fix: Add a live footer summary: "13 of 32 permissions. Opens: Today, Reservations, Arrivals... Can post payments, can see payroll." Warn on zero permissions; mark the four or five high-impact keys. This is a new element, so it is a proposal.

where: /en/people roster, 1440px and 375px
observed: People are still identified by email only, with avatar initials cut from the address. The account menu knows real names ("Demo Owner", "Albaraa Zain") and HR records have first and last names, so the name exists but the roster does not show it. Search was added (old PEOPLE-09 partly fixed), but filters by role or Property and a name column are absent. With five test addresses this is harmless; with real staff on personal addresses the roster cannot be read at a glance.
expected: The roster shows the person's name, with the address beneath it, and can filter by role and Property.
suggested_fix: Show the display name (falling back to the address) in the Person column, add role and Property filters.

where: /en/reservations > New reservation > Which unit?, dates Oct 28 to Oct 30, 1440 x 900
observed: After choosing dates the unit list shows four rooms (101 to 104, all FREE) and the line '38 more units. Type to find one.' There is no count of free units, no filter by type, no price per night on the rows, and nothing about readiness. A caller asking 'do you have a room for the 28th to the 30th, and how much?' is answered by the first four room numbers. Front-office FO-04 (2026-10-22) found the opposite problem (all 42 listed unsorted); the cap of four is new.
expected: The dialog says at once how many units are free for these nights, per type, with the nightly price, and lets the desk pick a type before a unit.
suggested_fix: Show 'N free: Room x 31 at TRY 2,800, Suite x 7 at ...' above the list, offer type chips, default to the first free unit of the chosen type, keep search for a specific number.

where: /en/reservations at 768 and at 375 px (emulated mobile)
