Stay, Unit, Price and Status are off to the right and the sticky '...' sits on top of the Stay dates. 375 px: only the Guest name, contact and '...' are visible per row; dates, unit and status need a sideways scroll inside the table. The bottom nav bar covers the last row until you scroll.
expected: On a phone each booking shows guest, dates, unit and status without a sideways scroll.
suggested_fix: Below 768 px render rows as cards (name, dates, unit, status chip, actions); the table stays for wide screens.

where: /en/reservations > row '...' and detail sheet for an in-house guest due today (Camila Torres, 102)
observed: The row menu and the sheet's menu for a checked-in guest offer Open folio, Show on the room map, Change departure, Move Guest. There is no Check out, and the sheet shows no balance or amount owed (Price: 'No price'). To check out the desk leaves Reservations for Departures. Front-office FO-08 reported the missing check-out and balance on the sheet; still absent.
expected: A guest who is due out today or overdue has a Check out action on the row and the sheet shows what they owe.
suggested_fix: Add 'Check out' (the Departures command, same review dialog) to the in-house row and the sheet; show balance beside Open folio.

where: any workspace route, /en, 375 px wide, bottom dock
observed: On a phone the Owner's navigation is a bottom dock with 15 items in a 1208 px scroller inside a 351 px window: about 4 items are visible and Audit log, Data export and Configuration need about three swipes. Nothing says there is more except the clipped last label ("Mai").
expected: The pages used most are one tap away; the rest sit behind a visible More.
suggested_fix: Dock shows Today, Front Office, Housekeeping, Finance and a More button that opens the full list in a sheet.

where: /en/today as Finance (28 attention items) and Front Desk Overview (33), 1440 px
observed: 'Needs attention' leads with another department's work. Finance: three 'Urgent repair' cards (102, 209, 202), one overdue departure card, then '24 more'; the money cards the role works from (20 overdue with a balance, TRY 69,875.00) are below or behind the button. Front Desk Overview: Days not closed, Room not ready, Can't check in, two Urgent repairs, then '28 more', so the 22 overdue departures are not on the strip at all.
expected: Attention for a role starts with that role's own items (money for Finance, departures and arrivals for the desk); other departments' items follow.
suggested_fix: Order attention by the viewing role's focus first, then by urgency; show the first item of each kind rather than the first four of the global list.

where: /en/today default Timeline, 1440 px; 2 arrivals, neither with an expected time, 312 dirty and 402 blocked
observed: Checking a guest in is the desk's most frequent job, and the default layout does not offer it. The timeline chart is empty ('No arrival has a time in this window') because neither arrival has a time. The two guests are plain text under the chart, linking to Arrivals. In the plan they rank 23rd and 24th behind 22 overdue departures, with 'Open Housekeeping' only. To check Mehmet Kaya in without leaving Today: open the layout switcher, choose House map (2 clicks; his arrival is preselected), press Check in, then Check in anyway = 4 clicks. From the default view the only path is a link out to Arrivals.
expected: Arrivals the desk can act on are on the first screen of the default layout, with Check in or the next fix beside the name, not behind 22 departure rows.
suggested_fix: When no arrival has a time, drop the empty chart and list arrivals as rows above the due-out list with the same action buttons; give a not-ready room the same inline 'Check in anyway' the House map already uses.

where: /en/today Timeline, 1440 px, 22 overdue
observed: The same 22 guests appear twice in one page, each with its own Check out button: in 'Due out today' (6 of 27 shown, 21 behind 'Show 21 more') and again in 'Do these in order' (5 shown, 19 behind 'Show 19 more'). Opening both makes a page about 4,500 px tall; two copies of every row make it unclear which list is the one to work. The 10-22 front-office report raised the same duplication (FO-17).
expected: One list of departures, with arrivals and room fixes as the plan around it.
suggested_fix: Let the plan list only what the due-out list does not (arrivals, rooms at risk, close the day) or fold the due-out list into the plan.

where: /en/today first open on a new device or browser, Manager and Owner
observed: A Manager and an Owner land on the front desk Timeline (the default for every desk focus). The manager's own view (attention strip, booked-ahead line, recent activity, charges today, maintenance counts) is only in 'Overview', two clicks away in a switcher whose hint reads 'The cards, as before'. The choice is a cookie per device (TL-DEF-04), so it has to be made again on every new browser and after clearing cookies. 'The cards, as before' means nothing to someone who never saw the old page.
expected: A manager's first screen is a manager's screen.
suggested_fix: Propose, do not build: default Manager and Owner to Overview (still changeable), and rename the hint 'Attention, activity, charges'. A saved preference per account (TL-DEF-04) removes the repeat.

where: /en/today at 375 px, Front Desk
observed: On a phone the header bar has no page title (the left half is empty) and the four headline figures fill the first screen at about 800 px; 'Today's flow' starts about 790 px down and the first Check out button about 1,000 px down. Touch targets, names and buttons are fine and nothing scrolls sideways at 375 or 768. The bottom dock scrolls sideways and clips 'Maintenance' as 'Mai' with no hint.
expected: The first action visible on the first screen, a page title, a visible edge to the dock.
suggested_fix: On narrow screens compact the figures to a single row and put the due-out list above them; show 'Today' in the bar.

where: Check-out dialog for Derya Polat, TRY 7,330 owing
observed: When a guest owes money the dialog offers 'Open the Folio in a new tab' and a required free-text reason (quick picks: Will pay later, Company invoice, Disputed). Taking the payment means leaving the dialog, paying on the Folio, returning and checking out again (the bill is checked again at confirm). Reaching the confirm takes 3 clicks (open, pick a reason, confirm) only if the guest does not pay; paying takes about 6 and a second tab. Same finding as FO-01 of 2026-10-22.
expected: A guest at the desk who pays by card is checked out in one place: amount prefilled from the bill, method, confirm.
suggested_fix: Propose, do not build: a 'Record payment' step inside the dialog, prefilled with the balance. Needs the owner's approval as a new interaction; Mews and Cloudbeds settle at check-out this way.

where: /en/today Timeline, 22 overdue departures with balances (20 of them owing)
observed: Clearing a large overdue list is one dialog per guest. Each dialog for a guest who owes needs a reason (required; quick picks 'Will pay later', 'Company invoice', 'Disputed') before 'Check out' enables. That is three clicks per guest at best (open, quick pick, confirm), about 66 clicks for 22. There is no select-several or 'same reason for all'. Verified for one guest, 22 times is inferred. On staging the overdue pile is unusual demo data; in a real hotel after a bad weekend or a stalled close it is a plausible morning.
expected: A bulk path for the cases where the gesture carries the information: select several, one reason, one confirm listing the total owed.
suggested_fix: Propose, do not build: checkboxes on due-out rows with a 'Check out N' bar that opens one dialog with the shared reason and the total balance (Mews and Opera Cloud both offer multi check-out).

where: /en/today, 1440 px, staging with at least eight other audit sessions loading it at the same time
observed: Server render of the page took 2.7 to 3.0 s in three fetches (about 279 KB), and /api/today, which polls every 60 s, took 2.7 to 2.9 s for 28 KB; the departures route took 0.34 s. October's audit measured about 10 s, so this is better, but it is still the slowest first screen I met. On first paint the due-out and plan rows for the Manager and Owner showed 'Open Departures' links, and the 'Check out' buttons replaced them after the client read finished, so the action arrives late and the row changes under the pointer. Timing is under shared load, so treat the seconds as an upper bound.
expected: First paint with the actions in under a second; a poll that does not cost three seconds of server time per open tab per minute.
suggested_fix: Profile the /api/today summary (all reads set-based, as in the ANALYZE fix), render the commands in the server HTML, and poll on a longer interval while the tab is hidden.

where: Close the day dialog, English
observed: Three sentences run together with no break: '...a booking with no price is not charged. No nights to charge Reopening a closed day is not available yet, so check the date before you close it.' The warning that a close cannot be reopened is the least visible line, in a grey box under the money text.
expected: Separate lines; the irreversibility line first or in its own notice.
suggested_fix: Render the three strings as separate paragraphs and move 'Reopening is not available yet' above the reason box.

where: /en/departures
observed: Two filter rows are stacked: a toggle (Due and overdue / Everybody in house) and chips (Due and overdue / Owing / Overdue and owing). 'Due and overdue' appears twice. With a chip active the banner offers 'Show all', the search offers 'Clear filters', and the chip row offers a third way back. A search for a guest who is in house but not due returns 'Nothing matches these filters.' without saying that Everybody in house would find them. Same as FO-10 of 2026-10-22.
expected: One filter row; a filtered-empty search says where else to look.
suggested_fix: Merge toggle and chips into one segmented control; on empty search offer 'Search everybody in house'.

where: Arrivals and Departures lists and dialogs, en and tr
observed: The column says Room; the dialogs say UNIT 312, UNIT 103 (Turkish: BİRİM 103 against column Oda). Every Departures row prints 'Guest stay' under the name, which carries no information for the usual case. 'Booking' and 'reservation' both appear.
expected: One word for the thing the desk hands over, and no constant label on every row.
suggested_fix: Use Room in the dialogs; show the stay type only when it is not a guest stay.

where: /en/arrivals, /en/departures (Housekeeping), /en/close-day (Finance), /en/rooms (Finance)
observed: Refusals name an internal permission that does not match the page: Departures says it needs "Take a booking" (Housekeeping), Close the day says "Close the day (end of the business day)". The text sends the person to 'someone who manages staff', not to the people who actually do the job (Front desk, Manager, Owner), and the page has no link onward beyond the top navigation. The explanation is present, which is better than the 2026-10-11 state.
expected: 'Departures is for Front desk, Manager and Owner. You can see your own work under Housekeeping.' with a link.
suggested_fix: Per page, name who uses it and offer one link to the closest page the role does have.

where: Check-out dialog confirm button when enabled (nothing owed)
observed: The enabled 'Check out' button is near-black with a dark arrow chip, so the arrow disappears; the button looks like a plain pill. The disabled state (grey) reads fine and its hint 'Add a reason to continue' says what is missing, which is good.
expected: The arrow keeps its contrast against the button.
suggested_fix: Give the arrow chip a lighter fill in the enabled state.

where: /en/rooms Add rooms dialog, first number '4O1' (letter O).
observed: The browser's own bubble 'Please match the requested format.' appears and the preview falls back to 'Enter the first room number to see what will be created'. The field hint says 'Digits only', but the error does not.
expected: The field says 'Use digits only, for example 401' inline.
suggested_fix: Replace the native validation with an inline message built from the same pattern.

where: /en/rooms, Add rooms dialog with a half-filled form, press Escape.
observed: Escape raises the browser's native confirm 'Discard the rooms you were about to add?' (OK / Cancel). It protects the input (good, fixes ROOMS-05) but looks unlike every other dialog on the screen and OK/Cancel do not say 'Discard' / 'Keep editing'.
expected: The same styled dialog as the rest of the app with 'Discard' and 'Keep editing'.
suggested_fix: Use the app's own confirm component.

where: /en/rooms: 'Rooms & beds', 'Bed map', 'Bed list' on a hotel where no room is let by the bed (all 42 rooms are whole rooms).
observed: The page and both view buttons speak of beds on a property that has none.
expected: Words follow the Property (RB-S1-11, filed): 'Room map' and 'Room list' when no room is let by the bed.
suggested_fix: Use the existing hasBeds flag to choose the labels.

where: /en/room-calendar filters ('Unit type', 'Unit state'), Move dialogs ('Move them to another Unit', 'Which unit', 'UNIT 103'), Rooms help text ('why this unit is unavailable').
observed: The page calls them rooms everywhere else but the filters and dialogs say Unit, and 'Guest' is capitalised mid-sentence ('Search a room or Guest', 'The Guest asked', 'Move Guest'). Turkish has the same split: 'Birim turu' next to 'Oda'. Blueprint vocabulary may require 'Unit' in code, but staff do not use it.
expected: One word for the thing, in sentence case.
suggested_fix: Use 'room' in staff-facing copy (EN, TR 'oda', AR 'غرفة'), lower-case 'guest'.

where: /en/room-calendar at 768 px with touch emulation, and the description line at 1280.
observed: The page says 'Drag a booking to another room or day to move it, or pull its end', and every bar's spoken description says 'Drag to move it', on a tablet where a touch on a bar scrolls and never drags (code: touch pointers are ignored; RC-S3-13 approves this). The phone layout hides the sentence, the tablet does not. The text never says what a touch user should do ('open the bar, then Move...').
expected: On touch screens the hint says 'Tap a booking, then Move...'.
suggested_fix: Choose the hint by pointer type (media query (pointer: coarse)).

where: /en/room-calendar and /en/rooms as Finance and as Housekeeping.
observed: The refusal is clear and the chips bar stays: 'Your role can't open this page. It needs the permission "Take a booking"...'. The page opens with any of five front-desk permissions, so naming one is misleading, and telling a housekeeper to ask for a booking permission invites a request that is wrong for the job.
expected: 'This page is for the front desk. Housekeeping has its own board' with a link to the page the role does have.
suggested_fix: Say who the page is for and link to the nearest allowed page (Housekeeping board, Departures).

where: /en/branding, no colour set
observed: With no colour saved the colour well shows a solid black swatch next to a placeholder '#0f5132', and the line under it says 'No colour set: Ranza's own theme is used.' The black swatch reads as 'black is chosen'; the code feeds the well '#000000' when the field is empty.
expected: An unset colour looks unset.
suggested_fix: Show an empty or checkered swatch, or the default theme green, until a colour is typed.

where: /en/branding after typing ffeb3b or e67e22, en and ar
observed: The colour check speaks in engineer terms: 'Text on filled surfaces is black, at 17.2 : 1.' and 'Links and text use a darker shade of the same hue so they stay readable on white: #847700 (4.5 : 1).' A hotel owner has to decode contrast ratios and a second hex code that they did not choose. The live preview itself is good and carries the real meaning.
expected: Say what happens in plain words and leave the numbers to a details line.
suggested_fix: 'Buttons use this colour with black text. Links use a slightly darker shade (#847700) so they stay readable.' and move the ratios behind a 'details' disclosure.

where: /ar/branding and /en/branding; native file input
observed: The logo field is the browser's own file control. In the Arabic page it reads 'No file chosen Choose File' in English and in the wrong order, and in every language it is unstyled next to the rest of the form. It also shows no thumbnail until a file is chosen and has no drop target.
expected: A localized, styled picker that names the file.
suggested_fix: Replace with a styled button using the page's locale, showing the file name, size and dimensions (see CONFIGURATION-01). A drop zone would be a new interaction; propose it separately.

where: /en/configuration at 375 px, Maintenance card
observed: The 'This Property' selects cut their current value with an ellipsis: 'Use the Organization's (When its req…'. Nothing runs past the card edge any more, but the setting's current value cannot be read on a phone without opening the select.
expected: The value is readable when the control is closed.
suggested_fix: Shorten the labels ('Same as Organization: When its request is done') or let the trigger wrap to two lines.

where: /ar/configuration, Time zone select
observed: The time zone is shown as 'Istanbul, تركيا · غرينتش+3': the country and offset are Arabic but the city stays Latin. In English the name is localized ('Istanbul, Türkiye'), so Arabic and Turkish readers get a mixed-script label.
expected: The city is named in the reader's language, as the currency already is.
suggested_fix: Use Intl.DisplayNames or a city-name table for ar and tr.

where: /ar/configuration, Housekeeping and Maintenance cards
observed: Arabic uses two words for Property on one page: 'المنشأة' (headings, 'Save for this Property' button, 'لهذه المنشأة') and 'العقار' (Maintenance selects, 'هذا العقار'). One word per concept is the product rule.
expected: One Arabic word for Property throughout.
suggested_fix: Pick 'المنشأة' (used in the page's own headings) and replace 'العقار' in the maintenance strings.

where: /en/configuration, 'Managed on their own screens'
observed: The 'People' link goes to /en/people with no ?property=, while 'Rooms & beds' keeps the Property. The Property context is dropped (ADR 0035 says keep the active Property).
expected: Both links keep the Property.
suggested_fix: Build the link with the same helper as 'Rooms & beds'.

where: Account menu, all pages
observed: Security is reachable only from the account menu (avatar, then Security), two clicks, and is not in the sidebar. The Owner and Manager sidebars list Configuration, Branding, Data export and Audit log but not Security.
expected: A person can find where to turn on two-step verification without already knowing the menu.
suggested_fix: Add Security to the sidebar's System group, or a one-line link on Today for an Owner whose two-step verification is off.

where: /en/security
observed: The page summary reads 'Manage how your account is signed in to.' (ungrammatical). The page is titled Security but holds only the two-step verification switch: no password change, no list of signed-in devices, no sign out everywhere. Those are recorded as not built (OA-NB-02, OA-NB-03), so the page title promises more than it holds.
expected: Copy that reads as a sentence, and a title that matches the content.
suggested_fix: 'How you sign in to Ranza.' and, until the other parts exist, a line that says password change and sessions are not available yet and whom to ask.

where: /en/audit-log, 1440 px
observed: The table row highlights on hover as if it were a link, but only the action title ("Checked out", "Payment posted") opens the record. Clicking the time, place, person or reason cell does nothing; verified in the DOM: the row has no click handler and one link in the What cell. Every lookup needs aim at the 100 px title.
expected: Anything that looks clickable opens the record, so the whole row is the target.
suggested_fix: Make the row's title link a stretched link (the row opens the record), keeping the subject link as its own target.

where: /en/audit-log, 59 records
observed: Most rows read "No reason required" in the Why column (about nine in ten of the 50 rows on page one). The few rows that carry a reason (a cancellation, a correction) are the ones the reader wants and they sit among identical grey text. The code comment says the label exists so an empty cell does not look like a missing reason.
expected: The rare rows with a reason stand out; a row that needs none is quiet.
suggested_fix: Show a dim dash with an accessible label 'No reason needed' for the common case, and keep the full words for rows where a reason was expected but is missing.

where: /en/audit-log, Why column on a 'Guest moved' record
observed: One Why cell starts with a code prefix: "guest_request: QA-C daha sessiz oda istedi ..." while sibling rows read plain sentences ("Guest asked to cancel"). The prefix looks like a stored reason code leaking into the text. Read as text; the source of the prefix (typed by the tester or produced by the app) is unknown.
expected: The Why column holds only the reason in words.
suggested_fix: Translate the reason code to a label ("Guest request") and show it before the free text, not as a raw key.

where: /en/audit-log, Who column
observed: Colleagues appear by email address ("frontdesk@prizic.com"), the viewer as "You". If the staff accounts had display names the code (names.labels) would show them; whether these demo accounts simply have none, or the lookup falls back to the email, I did not establish. For 'who changed this' a name is quicker to recognise than an address; an address does identify uniquely.
expected: A colleague appears by the name the roster shows, with the address available on hover or in the detail.
suggested_fix: Resolve the display name first and keep the email as the secondary text; ask the owner to confirm the demo accounts have names.

where: /en/audit-log and /ar/audit-log, list header and record detail
observed: The list header names the clock with a raw IANA id: "When (Europe/Istanbul)", which in Arabic reads "الوقت (Europe/Istanbul)" with the Latin id inside an RTL header. The single-record view shows "When  Oct 23, 2026, 23:52" with no zone at all, so a reader who opens a record from a link does not learn which clock it is. The fixed list sentence is under the table, not on the record.
expected: Both views say whose clock the time is, in words ("Demo Otel İstanbul time").
suggested_fix: Use the Property name in the header and add the same hint under 'When' on the record.

where: /en/audit-log, page one of 59 records, 50 per page
observed: Paging is one-way: a single 'Older records' button (cursor link); once on a later page a 'Newest' button returns to page one and there is no 'Newer'. Both links exist in the DOM; I did not follow 'Older'. For a large Organization (thousands of records) the only quick way back in time is the date filter. The record count is shown on every page. How the count performs at very large volume is unknown.
expected: Paging that can go back and forward, and a date jump.
suggested_fix: Add 'Newer records' beside 'Older records'; keep the date filter as the jump.

where: /en/data-export, Request an export, 375 and 1440 px
observed: 'Request export' is greyed until a dataset is ticked. The reason ('Choose at least one dataset.') is a small line under the heading near the top of the form; at 375 px the button is about 650 px lower and the reason is off screen. The button has no adjacent text and, from the code, no aria-describedby.
expected: The button says why it is off, next to it.
suggested_fix: Add 'Choose a dataset first' beside the button (or aria-describedby on it) while it is disabled.

where: /ar/data-export, Request an export
observed: One sentence in the Arabic form uses Arabic-Indic digits ("٥٠٠٠ تعني ٥٠٫٠٠", twice: in the Folios card and under File type) while every other number on the page and in the audit log is Latin ("7 أيام", "24 أكتوبر", "59 سجلًا"). Checked in the DOM: only those four tokens are Arabic-Indic. The digits are in the one sentence where a misread number costs money.
expected: One numeral set per page.
suggested_fix: Pass the example numbers through the same locale formatter as the dates, or write them as Latin digits in the Arabic string.

where: /en/finance?folio=<id> as Front desk, en
observed: Front desk sees the folio with Record payment only. Add a charge, the Reverse buttons and the Action column are simply absent and nothing says why or who can do it. A clerk who needs to fix a wrong minibar charge does not learn whether the button is missing, hidden or broken. (Showing the lines read-only to Front desk is the owner decision RANZ-56; recorded, not argued.)
expected: An absent action is explained in one line.
suggested_fix: Under the lines add 'Charges and reversals are done by Finance, a Manager or an Owner.'

where: /en/finance?folio=not-a-real-id and folio=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000, en
observed: The reported 500 is gone: both answer 200. They also answer silently. The folio list shows as if no folio had been asked for, the bad id stays in the address, and no message says 'that folio was not found'. A pasted link to a folio at another Property or one deleted by an export would look identical to the plain list.
expected: A folio link that cannot be opened says so and offers the list.
suggested_fix: Show a one-line notice 'That folio is not at this Property or does not exist' above the list and strip the id from the address.

where: /en/analytics?range=today, en
observed: RevPAR reads 'No available nights, so there is nothing to divide' while the same page shows 42 available nights (the true reason is that no day has closed). The badge reads '0 of 1 days closed' (should be '1 day'). The sibling card for ADR gives the right reason.
expected: The reason under a dash is the real reason.
suggested_fix: Reuse the ADR reason for RevPAR, and pluralise 'day' correctly in en, tr and ar.

where: Folio, list and Analytics in en, tr and ar
observed: Money is written three ways: English 'TRY 7,330.00', Turkish '₺7.330,00', Arabic '7,330.00 TRY' with Latin digits. The form label stays '(TRY)' in Turkish ('Tutar (TRY)') beside amounts written with the lira sign. The Arabic layout mirrors correctly (checked: dir=rtl, columns mirrored, dates in Arabic month names).
expected: One convention per language; the currency code appears once.
suggested_fix: Pick the Turkish convention for English too (symbol or code, not both styles), and drop '(TRY)' from labels where the amount field already shows the currency.

where: /en/portfolio as Owner and as Finance; Prizic Demo has one Property
observed: The empty state says: 'You have one Property, Demo Otel İstanbul. Properties line up side by side here once you are assigned to more than one. Ask an Owner if you should be assigned to another.' It is shown to the Owner too, who is the person being told to ask. The page is also not in any rail or chip bar (offered only with two or more Properties), so on staging it is reachable by typing the address. Everything past this state (cards, sort, money owed coverage, stale-id message) could not be observed.
expected: An Owner is told what an Owner can do.
suggested_fix: For Owner roles say 'Assign this Property's staff to another Property in People' or link to where Properties are added; keep 'Ask an Owner' for other roles.

where: /en/analytics typed into the address bar as Front desk, en
observed: The refusal is plain and complete, but names the permission as 'Read the general ledger' for a page called Analytics that shows occupancy and rates. A Front desk clerk cannot connect the two.
expected: The reason uses the words the page uses.
suggested_fix: Say 'It needs permission to see financial reports' (or name the page).

where: /en/housekeeping, 375 px, every row
observed: 'Report a problem' is a grey text link 121 x 19 px set directly under the room number and beside the 16 px select box (the box has a larger hidden hit area, the link does not). It repeats on all 42 rows, so a thumb aiming at the tick or the room can open the Maintenance form instead.
expected: Row controls on a phone are at least 44 px high and not stacked against each other.
suggested_fix: Move 'Report a problem' into the row menu (it is already one tap from there) or give it a 44 px target away from the tick box.

where: /en/guest-experience, 375 px
observed: The Open / Closed / All tab strip is 390 px of content in a 343 px scroller; 'All Requests' is cut off with no cue. The page itself no longer scrolls sideways.
expected: All three tabs visible, or an explicit scroll cue.
suggested_fix: Let the tabs share the width equally and drop the count pills below 400 px, or wrap as Maintenance's tabs do.

where: /en/guest-experience, /en/maintenance, English
observed: One concept, several words: the same action is 'Start Working' (button), 'In Progress' (status) and 'Move to In progress' (Maintenance); creating is 'New Request', 'Create service request' (eyebrow) and 'Log Request' (submit) on one dialog. Guest Experience uses Title Case ('Cancellation Reason', 'Resolution Notes', 'Log Request') where Maintenance uses sentence case ('New request', 'Move to Done'). Guest Experience also heads a column 'Reported At' where Maintenance says 'Reported 4 days ago'.
expected: One word per concept and one capitalisation across sibling screens.
suggested_fix: Pick 'Start' / 'In progress' / 'Done' and 'New request' everywhere; sentence case across both pages.

where: Maintenance request drawer and Settings tab, read-only roles
observed: A read-only drawer shows 'Assigned to' and 'Priority' as greyed dropdowns with chevrons that look like controls; the reason ('needs the permission to manage maintenance') is on the page behind the drawer, not in it. Finance's Settings tab shows six disabled selects and the reason only at the bottom of the panel.
expected: A control the role cannot use is shown as plain text with the reason beside it.
suggested_fix: Render read-only fields as text (value only) and put the one-sentence reason at the top of the panel or drawer.

where: Take room out of order, drawer, room with a Guest in house
observed: Before the first press the drawer says only 'Nobody will be able to sell it or check anyone into it until it returns to service'. The Guest in the room and the day they leave appear only after the first press (code: the first call returns an impact, the second press confirms with acknowledge=true; ImpactNotice). Room 209 is 'Guest in house' on the Housekeeping board and MT-7 holds it. The press that commits when there is no impact is a single, destructive-styled button. Not pressed here; judged from code.
expected: The consequence, including who is in the room, is named before the click.
suggested_fix: Load the occupant with the drawer and show it above the button ('Guest in house until Oct 26'); the confirm step then only repeats it.

where: /en/housekeeping, keyboard and screen reader, all widths
observed: The keyboard path to the common action works: the row's three-dot button is a real button, Enter opens the menu with focus on 'Mark clean', Escape closes it. But every row's tick box is labelled only 'Select row' (no room number, so a screen reader cannot say which room is being selected), each row adds three tab stops (tick, Report a problem, menu: 126 for 42 rooms) and the first row's menu is the 24th tab stop on the page. The three-dot buttons do carry the room ('Actions for 312').
expected: Every control names its room, and a keyboard user can reach and mark a room without crossing every other row.
suggested_fix: Label the tick box 'Select room 312'; consider one tab stop per row with arrow keys inside the table.

where: /en/people > Invite, as Manager
observed: A Manager's Invite dialog omits the Owner role and the "Every Property" option without saying why: the role list is Finance, Front desk, Housekeeping, Manager. The roster does explain a blocked row ("Their role or reach is above yours"), so the explanation exists elsewhere in the same screen.
expected: The dialog says "Owner is not offered because it is above your role" where the option would be.
suggested_fix: Show a one-line hint under the role picker when roles were filtered out.

where: /en/people and /en/hr for roles without the permission, 1440px; chips mode for Finance and Housekeeping
observed: The refusal is clear and names the permission, but the next step is hard-coded to shipped role names: "Ask someone who manages staff in your Organization, Owners and Managers can". For HR the same sentence is used although the missing permission is "See staff records and payroll". An Organization that defines its own role with these permissions is described wrongly. In chips mode (Finance, Housekeeping) the refused page has no breadcrumb and no active chip, only the back arrow. The refused page answers HTTP 200 (verified by fetch), not 403.
expected: The next step names the people who actually hold the permission, or says "your administrator".
suggested_fix: Reword to "your administrator can add this permission to your role" and show the page title in the chips bar.

where: /en/people > What each role can do > Save changes (read from code; no Organization-authored roles on staging)
observed: The save confirm for edited roles names the role and how many people lose their session, and says they get the new permissions on next sign-in, which is the right consequence. It does not list which permissions were added or removed; the owner has to remember the grid. Retiring a held role is refused with "Give them another role first" without naming who holds it.
expected: The confirm repeats the diff (added, removed) and a retire refusal lists the holders with a link to the roster.
suggested_fix: Add the diff to the confirm; link the holders.

where: /en, /tr, /ar food-and-beverage and inventory, link at the foot of the placeholder card
observed: 'This screen's handover note' is a link to https://github.com/prizic/ranza/blob/main/docs/handover/operator-workspace-screens.md. It opens in the same tab (target empty), leaves the app, lands on a long developer table in English, and is 20 px tall. 'Blueprint 5.6' and 'Blueprint 5.7' are literal English strings inside the Turkish and Arabic pages, in internal vocabulary a hotel manager has never seen. I did not open the link; its target and attributes are verified, the page content is from the repo file.
expected: An operator sees nothing meant for developers. Any link that leaves the app opens in a new tab.
suggested_fix: Remove the handover link and the Blueprint number from the operator build (show them only in development), or translate the number into 'Specification 5.6' and open the link in a new tab with a 44 px target.

where: Portal /en/sign-in, /en/forgot-password, 375 px and 1280 px; touch target sizes
observed: Language menu items are 32 px tall (measured on the Portal sign-in menu). At 375 px 'Forgot your password?' is a 343 x 20 px link, the one control a stuck guest needs. The 404 button 'Go to my stay' is 36 px tall. The show-password button (44 px) and Sign in (52 px) are fine.
expected: 44 px minimum for anything a guest taps on a phone.
suggested_fix: Give the menu items and the two links min-h-11 (the language pill and the buttons already do).

where: Portal /en/rooms (any address that is not a page), 375 px, signed out
observed: The 404 is now the Portal's own, in the address's language, with a way back, which fixes the bare framework page. What is left: it carries no wordmark, no language switch and no back-to-sign-in, so a guest who mistyped an address sees an unbranded page; the browser tab reads just 'Ranza' (the sign-in and help pages have their own titles). 'Go to my stay' for a signed-out guest goes to sign-in.
expected: The page says whose it is (wordmark) and offers the language menu; the tab title says what happened.
suggested_fix: Render the 404 inside the same split auth frame as the help page, and give it a title 'Page not found'. For a signed-out visitor label the button 'Sign in'.

where: Portal /en/forgot-password and /en/reset-password?token=abc, language menu
observed: The help page is one component for two routes, and its language links are built from one fixed pattern, so choosing Turkish or Arabic on /reset-password?token=abc goes to /tr/forgot-password and drops the query. Today the page is static text, so nothing is lost; the day a reset form exists, switching language mid-reset drops the token.
expected: Language switch keeps the page and its query.
suggested_fix: Pass the current route name into Help and use it in hrefPattern; carry the search string.

where: Portal /en/sign-in, then 'Forgot your password?' (1 click), desktop and 375 px
observed: The link opens a page whose only content is 'Resetting a password by email is not available yet. Ask the front desk at your property.' The sign-in page already says the same under the link ('No account, or can't sign in? Ask the front desk at your property.'). A guest who taps the link spends a click and a page load to read what was already on screen, and a link that says 'Forgot' promises a self-service flow that does not exist. The page also gives no way to reach the front desk (no number, no Property name), because the sign-in page does not know the Property.
expected: Until reset exists, the guest reads the answer where they are, once.
suggested_fix: Drop the link and keep the single help line, or keep the link and have it reveal the sentence in place. Name the real route (invitation email from the Property) when Portal activation exists.

where: Portal signed-in shell (every page, account menu, rail and top bar); /stay with a signed-in Resident; code and two evidence screenshots only
observed: The account menu is given the email as the display name (name={viewer.email} in the portal layout), so the corner shows 'e2e-resident-05...' truncated, and the same address is both name and email. The 2026-10-11 finding said the same and it is unchanged in the post-fix evidence image two-stays.png. Not seen live: there is no Resident login.
expected: A guest sees their own name, or at least the part before the @.
suggested_fix: Read the guest's name from the Stay record (there is one on the Reservation) and fall back to the local part of the email.

where: /en/reservations > New reservation > Email and Telephone
observed: One helper sentence ('Optional. An address already on file books that same Guest again instead of opening a second record.') sits under the Email and Telephone pair and is also attached to the Telephone input as its description. It is only true for email. A screen-reader user on Telephone hears an email rule.
expected: Each field has its own hint; Telephone says what format is expected and whether it is used to recognise a returning guest.
suggested_fix: Split the hint: email keeps its sentence; telephone gets its own (or none).

where: /en/reservations > Arriving today tab, 1440 x 900 with sidebar open
observed: The sticky action cell overlaps the Status column: the chips read 'Confirmed' and 'Requested' cut at the right edge, and the 'has to be confirmed' note wraps into a four-line sliver beside the '...' button.
expected: Status chip is whole; the action cell has a fixed width and its note truncates or moves under the row.
suggested_fix: Give the Status column a minimum width equal to its widest chip and cap the action cell's note to one line with a tooltip.

where: /en/reservations > Change departure dialog and the detail sheet, stay timeline
observed: The ruler labels skip days: for Oct 16 to Oct 24 it prints OCT 16, 17, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24 (18 and 22 missing) at uneven spacing, so the scale does not read as a calendar.
expected: Evenly spaced labels (every day, or every other day, or weekly) that never drop one day and keep the next.
suggested_fix: Pick a fixed label step from the number of nights and always include first and last.

where: /en/reservations search box at 1440 and 375 px
observed: The placeholder 'Search guest, room, reference, phone or date' is cut to '...phone or' at 1440 px and 'Search guest, room, ref' at 375 px, so the two most useful search keys (phone, date) are not announced.
expected: The box says what it searches without being cut off.
suggested_fix: Shorten to 'Name, room, phone, date' or let the box grow to fill the row.

where: /en/reservations as Finance and as Housekeeping (no Take a booking permission)
observed: Both see 'Your role can't open this page. It needs the permission “Take a booking”, and your role doesn't include it. Ask someone who manages staff ... to add it to your role.' It is explained and the navigation is chips without a Reservations link (good). But the page is a read list; the message sends a Housekeeping or Finance person to ask for the right to take bookings just to look one up, which neither role should want. No hint where they can see the same information (Departures for Finance).
expected: The denial names what the person can do instead, and does not suggest granting a booking right to read.
suggested_fix: Add a second line pointing to the page that serves the role (Finance: Folio; Housekeeping: Rooms) and drop the 'ask to be granted' wording for read-only needs.

where: /tr and /ar new reservation dialog and list
observed: Both locales render complete and mirror correctly in RTL, and the dialog's close label is translated (RES-15 fixed). Remaining word drift: Turkish asks 'Hangi oda?' (which room) in the dialog while the column is 'BIRIM' (unit); Arabic labels the person 'اسم النزيل' (resident/guest name) but the stay type 'إقامة ضيف' (guest stay).
expected: One word per concept in each language.
suggested_fix: Pick one Turkish word (oda or birim) and one Arabic word (ضيف or نزيل) for the person across the dialog and the list.

where: /en/audit-log as Front desk, Finance and Housekeeping; /en/finance?property=garbage as Owner; /en/integrations as Owner and Manager
observed: The same kind of refusal is worded four ways. Pages answer a bad ?property= with "That Property isn't one you can open" and a Go to Today button, but Finance answers "Finance is not open at this Property ... once your Organization's Subscription includes it", with no button, to an Owner whose Subscription includes it (neutral refusal FO-S9-01 by design). Audit log has its own "You can't read the audit log". Integrations, off at this Property, tells the Owner to "ask your Organization's Owner to request it" when the viewer is the Owner.
expected: One refusal pattern: a title, one reason in plain words, one next action.
suggested_fix: Route Finance and Audit log through the shared refusal component; say "You are the Owner: switch it on under Configuration" when the viewer is the Owner.

where: /en/food-and-beverage and /en/inventory
observed: Two rail entries open a page that holds one sentence under a PLANNED label, plus a link "This screen's handover note" and "Blueprint 5.6". The link goes to docs/handover on github.com/prizic/ranza (the host was read, the page was not opened). That is developer vocabulary to a hotel owner, and a repository link they probably cannot open. They are the only entries the other roles never see.
expected: Either no rail entry until built, or a plain "Coming later" note with no developer link.
suggested_fix: Remove the handover and blueprint links from the production page; hide the entries until built.

where: icon-only collapsed sidebar: 768 px wide, and 1200 px wide on first load
observed: In the collapsed rail People and HR & Payroll share one icon (Users in lib/screens.ts), and Inventory shares Boxes with Integrations. At 768 px the rail is icons only, so two identical people icons sit one above the other and a person has to hover to tell them apart. Tooltips on hover were not checked; accessible names exist.
expected: Each page has its own icon.
suggested_fix: Give HR & Payroll and Inventory their own icons (for example Briefcase, Package).

where: /en/sign-in after repeated attempts
observed: The limit message is clear ("Too many attempts. Try again in 7 seconds.") but is a fixed sentence. It does not count down and the Sign in button stays enabled, so the person presses it again into the same message.
expected: The countdown ticks and the button waits.
suggested_fix: Disable the button and tick the seconds, then clear the message at zero.

where: every workspace page, account menu and /en/security
observed: Security and Sign out are each two clicks away, through an account control that appears twice on desktop (sidebar footer and top-right avatar) and once in the chips bar. The Security subtitle reads "Manage how your account is signed in to."
expected: One account control; a sentence that parses.
suggested_fix: Keep one account control per layout; reword to "Manage how you sign in."

where: sign-in second step, for an account with two-step verification on
observed: The code field has autoComplete one-time-code but inputMode="text" (sign-in-form.tsx line 172), so a phone opens the full keyboard for a six-digit code. The field also takes a backup code, which is why. No test account has two-step on, so the step was not seen.
expected: Numeric keypad for a six-digit code, or a Use a backup code switch.
suggested_fix: Default to inputMode numeric, with a link that switches to text for a backup code.

where: ADR 0056 text against the live matrix, Manager on /en/branding
observed: ADR 0056 says "Owner and Manager, everything". The Manager is not offered Branding, and /en/branding refuses with branding.manage. The ADR table lists Branding as unchanged, so the behaviour is probably intended and the sentence is loose. Every other cell of the matrix agrees with the ADR (Housekeeping 4 pages, Finance 6, Front desk 6 groups plus 5, chips at six or fewer). ADR 0056 is still marked Proposed.
expected: The ADR and the screen say the same thing.
suggested_fix: Amend the sentence to say Manager reaches everything except Branding, or give Managers Branding.

where: chips bar, 375 px wide, /en/housekeeping
observed: The chips row scrolls sideways and the current page's chip is cut off at the edge ("Housel..."), with Maintenance out of sight. The cut-off hints that the row scrolls, but the active page is not brought into view.
expected: The active chip is fully visible on load.
suggested_fix: Scroll the active chip into view when the row mounts.

where: /en/today House map, arrival 312 (Dirty), 1440 px
observed: The House map offers 'Check in' on an arrival whose room is Dirty; pressing it opens an inline 'This room isn't ready yet. Not now / Check in anyway' (I stopped before 'Check in anyway'). Timeline and Next up withhold check-in for the same guest. The approved row TL-S2-04 says check-in is not offered where the room is not ready, so the code and the row disagree, and the layouts disagree with each other.
expected: One behaviour for a not-ready room in every layout. The House map's inline warning is the better pattern: it names the consequence and costs one click.
suggested_fix: Decide the rule, update TL-S2-04 or the House map, and make all three layouts behave the same.

where: /en/today Next up layout, 1440 px, 24 waiting items
observed: 'Waiting on you' lists all 24 items unfolded while the Timeline plan folds at 5. The dark card on the left stretches to match, so it is about 1,800 px tall with only a title, one sentence and two rows in its top fifth and the rest empty green. Arrow buttons at the bottom of that card, the only way to step through items, sit near the bottom of the page.
expected: Next up shows one thing at a time as designed, with its action in view.
suggested_fix: Fold the queue to 5 with 'Show more' as the Timeline does; do not stretch the featured card to the queue's height; put the next/previous arrows beside the title.

where: /en/today House map, 1440 px
observed: Room tiles are buttons whose accessible name is only '403, In house'; the visible 'Leaves', 'Overdue' and the guest name are not in it, so a screen-reader user hears a grid of identical-sounding states. Guest names are cut at about 12 characters on the tile ('Rauf Mam...', 'QA-A Early...') with no title or tooltip. In the status chips row '27 Still to leave' wraps to a second line at 1440 px.
expected: Name = room, guest, state; truncated text reachable on hover or focus.
suggested_fix: Put guest and state into the aria-label and a title; allow two-line names on the tile.

where: /en/today Timeline (bottom right) and Night desk, 13 days unclosed
observed: The 'Days not closed' card says '13 days waiting to be closed' and draws eight date pills (11 to 18) with nothing to say five more exist. The row is aria-hidden and capped at 8 in code (DAYS_SHOWN).
expected: A '+5' pill or a range ('Oct 11 to Oct 23').
suggested_fix: Add the overflow pill or replace the pills with a date range.

where: /en/today as Finance, 1440 px
observed: Two of the four tiles share the eyebrow 'All Folios' ('30 open Folios' and 'TRY 66,335.00 balance across open Folios') and open the same list. The same names appear twice again below: 'Leaving with a balance' (25) and 'Largest open balances' (5) repeat the same guests. At 1440 the big figures ('TRY 92,160.00', 'TRY 66,335.00') run to the card edge. The tile 'Balance on today's departures' counts the 22 overdue guests as well as the 5 leaving today.
expected: Each tile named for what it counts (TD-S7-09), with figures inside the card.
suggested_fix: Merge the two Folio tiles into one ('30 open Folios, TRY 66,335.00'); rename the departures tile 'Owed by departing and overdue Guests'; reduce figure size one step.

where: /en/today Overview, 'Recent activity', Manager
observed: Each activity row shows the actor as the login name ('frontdesk') with the initial 'F', while the greeting and the account menu use display names ('Demo Front Desk'). Three rows, all from Oct 23.
expected: The person's display name, as everywhere else.
suggested_fix: Resolve the actor label to the display name when the activity feed is built.

where: /en/today Timeline axis, 1440, 768 px, around 13:00
observed: The 'Now' marker sits on top of the first hour label, so the axis reads '13:' or '13:0' (clipped by the pill) and the first tick cannot be read.
expected: Tick labels are always readable.
suggested_fix: Hide the tick label under the marker or move the marker above the axis.

where: /en/today, layout switcher copy and Night desk
observed: Layout names and hints are ambiguous to a new user: 'Overview: The cards, as before', 'Next up: One thing at a time', 'Night desk: Closing and hand-over'. 'Night desk' is offered at 13:00 and draws a dark surface that departs from the palette (TL-S1-10, still waiting for the owner). The switcher shows no preview and does not say it is saved on this device.
expected: Names that say what is in them: 'Cards', 'One at a time', 'Close and hand over'; a line saying 'Saved on this device'.
suggested_fix: Reword hints; add the saved-on-this-device line under the list.

where: /en/today Night desk as Manager, 1440 px, 'Next seven nights'
observed: The seven-night bar chart is wider than its card: the 'FRIDAY' label and its '0' run past the card's right edge. The chart also lists no dates, only weekday names, so 'Saturday' could be today or next week; the first bar (25) is tonight.
expected: A chart that fits its card and names the dates (Sat 24, Sun 25 ...).
suggested_fix: Let the columns shrink to the card width, abbreviate weekday names, add the day number.

where: /en/data-export, History
observed: From the code: History lists the 50 most recent requests and has no paging, filter or search ('The 50 most recent requests for Prizic Demo'). With a daily schedule plus manual requests, older failed or expired records fall off the list, and there is no way to show only failed ones or only mine. Files are removed after 7 days anyway, so the effect is on the record, not on files. Staging had zero exports, so the cap was not seen.
expected: I can find a failed export from last week, or filter to my own.
suggested_fix: Add a 'Failed only' and 'Mine' toggle and an 'Older' link.

where: /en/hr?tab=leave, Approve / Decline dialog
observed: Leave decisions now have a confirm (fixes the old one-click), but the copy says "A decision is final: it cannot be changed afterwards, and the employee is not told from here, so tell them yourself." There is still no reason field and no undo, and a mis-click on Decline means a conversation. Read from code; staging has no leave requests.
expected: A declined request carries a reason the employee can be told, or can be reopened within a short window.
suggested_fix: Add an optional reason on Decline; allow the deciding manager to reopen for 24 hours as People does for access removal.
